items.action: Extend any existing Managed Agents integration to use the memory layer before building a custom persistence layer. The filesystem model means you can inspect, edit, and version agent memory with standard file tools, which is a significant ops advantage over embedding-based memory systems.

items.headline: OpenAI releases Privacy Filter as open-weight Apache 2.0 model for on-device PII detection
items.description: OpenAI published Privacy Filter on April 22, an open-weight 1.5B-parameter sparse model with 50M active parameters per forward pass, designed for high-throughput PII detection and redaction directly on device. It achieves a 96% F1 score across eight privacy categories including names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, and account numbers, and processes long inputs in a single pass without sending data to any API. The model is available under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and GitHub, allowing commercial use and fine-tuning without royalties or copyleft requirements.
items.action: Add Privacy Filter as a preprocessing step in any pipeline where user-provided text reaches a cloud model. The on-device execution model means sensitive data can be sanitized before it crosses a trust boundary, which is a compliance win for healthcare, legal, and finance clients.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.119 adds config persistence, multi-platform PR review, and hooks timing data
items.description: Released April 23 at 23:24 UTC, v2.1.119 makes /config settings persist to ~/.claude/settings.json with a full project/local/policy override precedence chain. The --from-pr flag now accepts GitLab, Bitbucket, and GitHub Enterprise PR URLs in addition to GitHub.com, and a new prUrlTemplate setting lets teams point code-review links at any host. Hooks now receive duration_ms in PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure events, enabling timing-based automation and alerting. PowerShell tool commands can be auto-approved in permission mode on Windows.
items.action: Upgrade to 2.1.119 if your team uses GitLab or Bitbucket for code review, as --from-pr now works natively across platforms. Add duration_ms logging to PostToolUse hooks to identify slow tool calls in long agentic sessions.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.124.0 adds TUI reasoning controls, multi-environment app-server, and Bedrock auth
items.description: Released April 23 at 18:29 UTC, v0.124.0 stable introduces keyboard shortcuts for controlling reasoning depth directly in the TUI without editing config, support for multiple named environments in app-server sessions so teams can switch contexts within one session, and AWS Bedrock authentication for OpenAI-compatible provider configurations. Hooks can now be configured inline as stable config rather than external scripts, and eligible ChatGPT plans default to the Fast service tier.
items.action: Use the multi-environment flag in app-server sessions to separate dev, staging, and production contexts in long-running Codex agents without restarting the session. Test inline hook configuration for simpler CI pipeline integration.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.35 stable adds named sessions and slash command argument tab-completion
items.description: Released April 23 at 23:24 UTC, v1.0.35 stable makes slash commands fully tab-completable including arguments and subcommands, which significantly reduces typing in long sessions. Sessions can now be named with --name and resumed by name, replacing the previous UUID-based resume flow. Ctrl+Y is added as an alternative to Tab for accepting highlighted options in completion popups.
items.action: Adopt --name for sessions in shared team environments where multiple engineers hand off the same context. Slash command tab-completion makes the tool meaningfully faster in complex multi-step agent interactions.

2026-04-25.summary: DeepSeek launches V4 Pro and Flash as MIT-licensed open-weight models matching closed frontier performance at one-sixth the cost, GPT-5.5 API goes live for developers, and Claude Code 2.1.120 ships a CI-ready ultrareview subcommand.

items.headline: DeepSeek releases V4 Pro and Flash as MIT-licensed open weights rivaling GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 at a fraction of cost
items.description: DeepSeek open-sourced V4-Pro (1.6T-parameter MoE, 49B active per token) and V4-Flash (284B total, 13B active) simultaneously on April 24 under the MIT license with weights published to Hugging Face. Both models expose a 1M-token context window natively, dual Thinking and Non-Thinking modes, and support both OpenAI and Anthropic API message formats out of the box. V4-Pro scores 80.6% on SWE-bench Verified at $1.74/$3.48 per million tokens; V4-Flash scores 79.0% at $0.14/$0.28, roughly one-sixth the cost of Opus 4.7 or GPT-5.5.
items.action: Test V4-Flash as a drop-in for high-volume agent loops where GPT-5.4 Mini or Gemini Flash served before. V4-Pro for near-frontier reasoning at significantly reduced cost. Migrate off deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner before their July 24, 2026 retirement.

items.headline: GPT-5.5 API goes live for all key holders one day after ChatGPT-only rollout
items.description: OpenAI confirmed on April 24 that GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro are now accessible via standard API keys, closing the gap from the day-prior launch that was limited to ChatGPT and Codex. Standard pricing is $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens; GPT-5.5 Pro is $30/$180. The updated system card describing API-specific safeguards was published alongside the availability announcement. The 1M context window and agentic computer-use capabilities are fully available to API callers.
items.action: Integrate GPT-5.5 into pilot workflows now that API access is live. At double GPT-5.4 pricing, benchmark quality gains against cost before swapping model IDs in production.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.120 ships CI-ready ultrareview subcommand and drops Windows Git Bash requirement
items.description: Released April 25 at 00:14 UTC, v2.1.120 adds the `claude ultrareview [target]` subcommand for non-interactive code review that prints findings to stdout and exits with a standard exit code, enabling direct CI pipeline integration. Windows installations no longer require Git for Windows as PowerShell is now the fallback shell tool. Skills can reference the current effort setting via `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}`, and the `AI_AGENT` environment variable is now propagated to subprocesses enabling GitHub traffic attribution to Claude Code.
items.action: Add `claude ultrareview` to your PR CI step for automated code review output. Update effort-sensitive Skills to use `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}`. Windows-only deployments can now drop Git for Windows as a prerequisite.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Rate Limits API for programmatic workspace quota monitoring
items.description: As of April 24, the Rate Limits API lets organization administrators query current rate limit configurations for their org and individual workspaces via a dedicated API endpoint. The response includes both Anthropic-set limits and any custom limits configured in the Console, removing the need for manual Console polling in capacity planning and alerting pipelines. The API is authenticated with standard API keys.
items.action: Wire the Rate Limits API into your observability stack. Replace manual Console checks with automated rate-limit headroom monitoring to catch capacity constraints before they affect production workflows.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.125.0 adds Unix socket app-server transport and persistent permission profiles
items.description: Released April 24 at 18:00 UTC, v0.125.0 brings stable app-server integrations using Unix socket transport for local inter-process communication without HTTP overhead. Permission profiles now persist across sessions so tool-access approvals survive process restarts and do not require re-granting on each launch. Model provider configuration is also updated in this release.
items.action: Upgrade Codex CLI to 0.125.0 if building local agent harnesses or app-server integrations. The persistent permission profile meaningfully reduces friction for multi-session developer workflows.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.36 adds keep-alive command and fixes silently broken custom instruction loading
items.description: Released April 24 at 18:39 UTC, v1.0.36 adds the `/keep-alive` command to maintain session context, introduces a double-Esc requirement to cancel in-progress work preventing accidental interruptions, and fixes a bug where custom instruction files stored in `.gitignored` directories were silently skipped and never applied. Subcommand picker selection indicators were also added.
items.action: Update to 1.0.36 immediately if you use custom `.claude` instruction files in gitignored directories, as those files have been silently failing to load in prior versions.

2026-04-26.summary: Gemini adds autonomous research agents with MCP support to its API; an LLM deployment toolkit sees active SSRF exploitation within hours of disclosure; OpenAI releases GPT-5.5 prompting guidance for API developers.

items.headline: Gemini adds Deep Research Max with MCP support and private data access to Interactions API
items.description: Google launched two new agent models via the Gemini API Interactions API on April 21: Deep Research (speed-optimized) and Deep Research Max (maximum comprehensiveness), both built on Gemini 3.1 Pro. The agents combine web search with private enterprise data sources via MCP servers in a single API call, returning fully cited reports with embedded charts. Access is via paid Gemini API tiers using model IDs deep-research-preview-04-2026 and deep-research-max-preview-04-2026.
items.action: Explore the Interactions API for automated research pipelines; test MCP connector integration to route private data sources alongside web search for enterprise knowledge workflows.

items.headline: LMDeploy SSRF flaw exploited within 13 hours of disclosure affecting VLM inference servers
items.description: CVE-2026-33626, a high-severity (CVSS 7.5) server-side request forgery vulnerability in LMDeploy vision-language image loader, was disclosed April 21 and actively exploited within 13 hours. Attackers used the load_image() function to probe internal networks, cloud metadata services, Redis, and MySQL from VLM inference endpoints. All LMDeploy versions prior to 0.12.3 are affected.
items.action: Upgrade LMDeploy to 0.12.3 immediately. Add network-level controls restricting outbound HTTP from VLM inference servers to known-safe hosts.

items.headline: OpenAI publishes GPT-5.5 prompting guide as API goes live
items.description: OpenAI published dedicated GPT-5.5 prompting guidance on April 25, the day after the API opened to all key holders. The key directives: treat GPT-5.5 as a new model family requiring a fresh baseline rather than a drop-in replacement; use shorter outcome-oriented prompts; avoid over-specified process instructions that narrow the model search space. Legacy instruction stacks from GPT-5.4 or earlier can degrade performance on this model.
items.action: Before migrating production GPT-5.4 integrations to GPT-5.5, review the official guide and benchmark a minimal fresh-baseline prompt against your existing instruction stack.

2026-04-27.summary: Anthropic admits three engineering changes quietly degraded Claude Code quality for a month; Dispatch persistent desktop agent rolls out to Max subscribers; and a LangChain text splitter SSRF flaw exposes cloud metadata endpoints.

items.headline: Anthropic confirms three engineering changes behind month-long Claude Code quality drop
items.description: Anthropic published a postmortem identifying three changes that compounded into a significant quality regression affecting Claude Code, the Agent SDK, and Cowork from early March through April 20: default reasoning effort was silently downgraded from high to medium on March 4, a caching bug introduced March 26 incorrectly cleared thinking history every turn instead of once per idle session, and a verbosity prompt added April 16 was found to reduce coding quality before being reverted April 20. All three issues were resolved as of v2.1.116 and Anthropic reset usage limits for all subscribers on April 23. The API itself was not affected; only harness-level changes triggered the degradation.
items.action: Update Claude Code to v2.1.119 or later to ensure all fixes are active. Test any agentic workflows that regressed in March or April against a fresh session to confirm quality is restored. Consider pinning reasoning effort to high explicitly in your CLAUDE.md if silent defaults matter to your workload.

items.headline: Claude Dispatch persistent desktop agent rolls out to Max plans today with computer use in Cowork
items.description: Anthropic is rolling out Dispatch, a persistent agent thread bridging the Claude mobile app to Claude Desktop, to Max plan subscribers starting April 27 with Pro plans following within two days. Claude can open files, run dev tools, click and navigate on screen with no additional setup, allowing users to assign desktop tasks from their phone and return to find them completed. The feature makes Claude a 24/7 background desktop agent for knowledge work without any code or infrastructure requirement.
items.action: Enable computer use in Claude Desktop on your Pro or Max plan. Try assigning a multi-step file preparation or browser-based research task via the mobile app while away from the desk to validate the Dispatch loop.

items.headline: LangChain text splitter SSRF flaw lets attacker controlled redirects reach cloud metadata endpoints
items.description: CVE-2026-41481 in langchain-text-splitters before 1.1.2 allows an attacker-controlled server to redirect HTMLHeaderTextSplitter.split_text_from_url() to internal, localhost, or cloud provider metadata endpoints after the initial URL passes validation, because redirect targets are not revalidated. Successful exploitation can expose AWS EC2 instance metadata, GCP service account tokens, and any credentials available at internal endpoints. The fix is in langchain-text-splitters 1.1.2, published April 24, 2026.
items.action: Pin langchain-text-splitters to 1.1.2 or later immediately. Audit any pipeline that passes user-supplied or externally-sourced URLs to HTMLHeaderTextSplitter, especially if those pipelines run in cloud environments with IMDSv1 enabled or without metadata endpoint firewall rules.

2026-04-28.summary: Claude Code adds persistent MCP server loading and hook-based tool output interception; DeepSeek slashes cache hit pricing to one-tenth across all API models; and Copilot CLI ships shell script generation with location-aware permission persistence.

items.headline: Claude Code adds persistent MCP tool loading and hook-based tool output replacement
items.description: Version 2.1.121, released April 28, introduces alwaysLoad in MCP server config to permanently bypass tool-search deferral for trusted servers, so their tools are always available without selection overhead. PostToolUse hooks can now replace any tool's output before it reaches the model via hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput, enabling centralized output sanitization and transformation. The claude plugin prune command removes orphaned auto-installed plugin dependencies, and a type-to-filter search box lands in the skills panel.
items.action: Add alwaysLoad: true to MCP servers you always need in production, removing the tool-search selection step. Wire PostToolUse hooks to standardize or sanitize tool outputs before they enter the context window.

items.headline: DeepSeek cuts cache hit API pricing to one-tenth across all models as price war intensifies
items.description: DeepSeek announced April 27 that input cache hit fees across its entire API lineup have been reduced to one-tenth of their original price, applying to deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner, V4-Pro, and V4-Flash. The move coincides with a 75 percent limited-time discount on V4-Pro through May 5. Bloomberg reported the announcement triggered stock drops at competing Chinese AI providers Zhipu and Minimax.
items.action: Cache hit pricing is the dominant cost lever in production agentic workflows that repeatedly send similar system prompts. Recalculate your DeepSeek infrastructure cost model with the new cache hit rates before committing to V4-Pro integrations.

items.headline: Copilot CLI gains shell script generation command and location-based permission persistence
items.description: Version 1.0.37, released April 27, ships the copilot completion subcommand for generating shell script completions and enables location-based permission persistence by default so approvals granted in a project directory carry forward across sessions. The session picker gains a sort key, cycling through relevance, last used, created, and name order by pressing s. Markdown rendering in ask responses and X11 handle leaks on Linux are also fixed.
items.action: Enable location-based permission persistence to eliminate repeated tool call approvals in established project directories. Use copilot completion to generate shell-native command completions for scripted CI workflows.

2026-04-29.summary: OpenAI ends Azure exclusivity and lands GPT-5.4 on Amazon Bedrock within 24 hours; Anthropic ships 9 MCP connectors spanning Adobe, Blender, and Autodesk; and Microsoft patches an Entra ID role flaw that let AI agents escalate to service principal takeover.

items.headline: OpenAI ends Azure exclusivity and ships GPT-5.4 on Amazon Bedrock the same day
items.description: Microsoft and OpenAI restructured their partnership on April 27, ending the exclusive Azure cloud commitment and making the IP license explicitly non-exclusive through 2032. Within 24 hours, GPT-5.4 went live in limited preview on Amazon Bedrock, with GPT-5.5, Codex, and OpenAI Managed Agents to follow. Bedrock access inherits native AWS controls including IAM, PrivateLink, CloudTrail logging, and guardrails, removing the need for a separate OpenAI API key management layer.
items.action: Test OpenAI model access through your existing Bedrock infrastructure. Teams already routing Anthropic and Gemini via Bedrock can now add GPT-5.4 without changing auth or billing architecture.

items.headline: Anthropic releases 9 MCP connectors spanning Adobe Creative Cloud, Blender, Autodesk, and Ableton
items.description: Anthropic launched MCP connectors for Adobe Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Premiere, Express plus 47 other apps), Blender, Autodesk Fusion, Ableton, Splice, Affinity, SketchUp, and Resolume, accessible through Claude Cowork and the Claude apps. The Blender connector enables analysing and scripting entire 3D scenes; the Adobe connector spans the full Creative Cloud portfolio. Anthropic simultaneously joined the Blender Development Fund as a patron to support the Python API used by the connector.
items.action: Enable the Adobe or Blender connector in Claude Cowork for any client running a creative production workflow. The Adobe connector bridges the 50-app Creative Cloud suite through a single MCP endpoint without custom integration work.

items.headline: Microsoft patches Entra ID agent role that let AI agents escalate to tenant-wide service principal takeover
items.description: Silverfort disclosed on April 28 that the Agent ID Administrator built-in role in Entra ID, introduced as part of Microsoft's agent identity platform, had scope overreach allowing any assigned user to become owner of arbitrary service principals beyond agent-related identities. Exploiting this on a privileged service principal could grant tenant-wide control. Microsoft patched the role scope on April 9 after Silverfort's March 1 report; Silverfort's public disclosure on April 28 confirmed 99 percent of enterprise tenants had at least one privileged service principal meeting the escalation conditions.
items.action: Audit all Agent ID Administrator role assignments in Entra ID tenants running AI agents. The Microsoft patch applied April 9 is server-side with no action needed, but any service principal that was compromised before that date should be reviewed for unexpected owners or credentials.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.122 adds Bedrock service tier selection and fixes structured output errors on Vertex AI
items.description: Version 2.1.122, released April 28, adds the ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER environment variable to select default, flex, or priority capacity tiers in Bedrock deployments. Pasting a PR URL into the /resume search now automatically finds the session that created that PR across GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket. Fixes resolve a Vertex AI and Bedrock structured-output 400 error and a Vertex AI count_tokens 400 behind proxy gateways.
items.action: Set ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER=priority in production Bedrock environments if capacity consistency is required. The /resume PR URL detection reduces context loss when returning to multi-repo agent sessions.

items.headline: n8n 2.18.4 graduates to stable with AI agent max steps raised from 5 to 60
items.description: The 2.18.x line reached stable status with version 2.18.4, released April 27. The AI builder orchestrator maximum steps ceiling increased from 5 to 60, enabling significantly longer autonomous agent runs without manual workflow continuation. The release also adds a computer use toggle to the chat sidebar, private npm package authentication for community node installations, and OIDC configuration via environment variables.
items.action: Update to n8n 2.18.4. The 12x increase in AI agent max steps removes the most common bottleneck in long-running automation workflows. Review any workflows that previously hit the 5-step limit and re-run with increased depth.

items.headline: Copilot CLI 1.0.39 adds ACP session permission mode toggle and background task execution
items.description: Version 1.0.39, released April 28, lets ACP clients toggle allow-all permission mode via session configuration without modifying global settings. New slash commands /compact, /context, /usage, and /env are available inside ACP sessions. Background task execution via Ctrl+X then B moves a running task to the background while continuing in the terminal, mirroring the Claude Code workflow.
items.action: Update to 1.0.39 and use the ACP session permission mode toggle for scripted environments where you want allow-all scoped to a single session rather than persisted globally.

2026-04-30.summary: Anthropic retires the 1M context window beta for Sonnet 4.5 and Sonnet 4 today, breaking calls above 200k tokens; Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.5-Pro open source model matches Claude Opus 4.6 on coding benchmarks at 40 to 60 percent lower token cost.

items.headline: Anthropic 1M context window beta retired for Sonnet 4.5 and Sonnet 4; requests above 200k now return errors
items.description: Effective today, the context-1m-2025-08-07 beta header no longer extends context windows for claude-sonnet-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-20250514. Any API call to these models exceeding 200k input tokens will return an error with no fallback. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Opus 4.6 support the full 1M token context window natively at standard pricing without a beta header.
items.action: Audit all API callers that send the context-1m-2025-08-07 beta header or pass more than 200k tokens to Sonnet 4.5 or Sonnet 4. Swap the model tag to claude-sonnet-4-6 or claude-opus-4-6 to restore 1M context access immediately.

items.headline: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo-V2.5-Pro under MIT, matching Claude Opus 4.6 on agentic coding at lower token cost
items.description: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.5-Pro as MIT open source: a 1.02T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 42B active parameters, a 1M token context window, and a hybrid-attention architecture. On ClawEval agentic benchmarks the model achieves 64 percent Pass cubed using 40 to 60 percent fewer tokens than Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4 at comparable quality. The model is available via API at one dollar per million input tokens and three dollars per million output tokens, and via Hugging Face for self-hosting. Xiaomi is running a 30-day 100 trillion token grant program for approved builders until May 28.
items.action: Evaluate MiMo-V2.5-Pro as a lower-cost executor model in agentic pipelines currently running Opus-class models. Apply for the 100T token grant at the Xiaomi MiMo Orbit site before May 28 if testing in production. The MIT license allows commercial use without restrictions.

2026-05-01.summary: OpenAI Codex CLI v0.128.0 ships persisted slash goal task workflows with app-server pause and resume controls; NVIDIA open-sources Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, a 30B multimodal model covering vision, audio, and text on 25 GB RAM.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex CLI v0.128.0 ships persisted goal workflows with app server pause and resume controls
items.description: Codex CLI v0.128.0, released April 30, is the first stable build with persistent /goal workflows: tasks survive process restarts and can be paused, forked, or resumed via new app-server APIs and TUI controls. The release also adds configurable terminal keymaps, expanded permission profiles with sandbox-aware built-in defaults, remote plugin bundle caching, and external agent session import for bringing sessions from other tools into Codex. MultiAgentV2 configuration is now explicit, giving orchestrators fine-grained control over subagent behavior.
items.action: Update to v0.128.0 and migrate long-running task automation from ephemeral sessions to /goal workflows. Review the new permission profile defaults to ensure sandbox CLI profiles match your security posture before enabling remote bundle caching.

items.headline: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3 Nano Omni open multimodal model combining vision speech and text on 25 GB RAM
items.description: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni is a 30B hybrid Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 3B parameters per token, combining vision, audio, and language in a single open model that fits in 25 GB of GPU memory. NVIDIA reports up to 9x higher throughput than comparable open omni models on video and document workloads and tops six leaderboards for complex document intelligence and video and audio understanding. The model is available via Hugging Face, OpenRouter, build.nvidia.com, and more than 25 partner platforms.
items.action: Evaluate as a single-model replacement for separate vision and speech pipelines in document intelligence or multimodal agent workflows. Available immediately on OpenRouter with pay-per-token pricing for rapid prototyping before committing to self-hosted deployment.

2026-05-02.summary: Google patches a CVSS 10.0 remote code execution flaw in Gemini CLI CI headless mode, Microsoft launches Agent 365 as a universal AI agent governance platform with native MCP tool controls, and Cursor IDE discloses a CVSS 9.9 git hook RCE patched in February.

items.headline: Google patches CVSS 10.0 remote code execution flaw in Gemini CLI CI headless mode
items.description: Gemini CLI versions below 0.39.1 contained a maximum severity RCE: in headless mode the tool automatically trusted any workspace folder, allowing an attacker to place a malicious GEMINI.md config file that executed commands on the host before the agent sandbox initialized, turning any CI pipeline running gemini headless into a supply chain attack surface. The flaw was discovered by Novee Security and Pillar Security and fixed in @google/gemini-cli 0.39.1 and 0.40.0-preview.3. Any automated code review or AI-assisted CI workflow using Gemini CLI on GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar was exposed.
items.action: Update Gemini CLI to 0.39.1 or later immediately. Audit CI pipelines that call gemini in headless mode for unexpected config files. Review workspace trust settings if you self-host Gemini agents.

items.headline: Microsoft Agent 365 launches as universal AI agent governance platform with native MCP tool controls
items.description: Microsoft Agent 365 is now generally available at $15 per user per month as a unified control plane for enterprise AI agents regardless of framework (Anthropic Claude Code SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, Copilot Studio, and any third-party implementation) or hosting provider (Azure, AWS, GCP, on-premises). Agents register via the Agent 365 SDK or CLI and expose standardized MCP interfaces; administrators can centrally view, allow, or block MCP tools tenant-wide and detect overprivileged maker credentials in agent configurations. Agent 365 is bundled in the new Microsoft 365 E7 Frontier Suite at $99 per user per month alongside M365 Copilot and Entra Suite, with local agent discovery and blocking entering preview.
items.action: If you build agents for enterprise clients on Microsoft 365, register agents via the Agent 365 SDK for centralized MCP tool governance and audit trails. Evaluate E7 bundle pricing versus standalone if your clients already pay for E5 plus Copilot.

items.headline: CVE-2026-26268 Cursor IDE CVSS 9.9 git hook RCE disclosed after February patch
items.description: Novee Security disclosed CVE-2026-26268, a CVSS 9.9 remote code execution vulnerability in Cursor IDE versions below 2.5: an attacker embeds a malicious pre-commit hook in a nested bare repository, which Cursor's AI agent triggers automatically during routine git operations such as checkout, executing arbitrary code on the developer's machine without user interaction or warning. The root cause is agentic git workflows operating on untrusted repositories without hook sandboxing. Patched in Cursor 2.5 in February 2026; public disclosure followed April 28 after coordinated disclosure.
items.action: Update Cursor to version 2.5 or later. Treat any cloned third-party repository as untrusted when using Cursor's AI-driven git features until the repo is audited.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.126 adds gateway model discovery and terminal OAuth paste for containerized installs
items.description: The model picker in Claude Code now queries the /v1/models endpoint from any Anthropic-compatible gateway when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set, enabling dynamic model selection on custom proxies and self-hosted deployments without hardcoding model IDs. A new claude project purge command deletes all project-level state including transcripts, tasks, file history, and config entries with dry-run and interactive safety modes. OAuth login now accepts codes pasted directly in the terminal, unblocking WSL2, SSH, and container environments where browser callbacks cannot reach localhost. A security fix corrects allowManagedDomainsOnly and allowManagedReadPathsOnly being silently bypassed when a higher-priority managed settings source lacked a sandbox block.
items.action: Update to 2.1.126 if running Claude Code behind a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway: the model picker now auto-discovers available models from your gateway. Use claude project purge for clean-slate resets in CI or ephemeral environments.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.40 adds client credentials OAuth for headless MCP server authentication
items.description: Copilot CLI v1.0.40 adds the client_credentials OAuth grant type for MCP servers, enabling fully headless server-to-server authentication without browser redirects for automated MCP orchestration pipelines. The release also adds automatic Azure DevOps repository detection with GitHub MCP server disabling to prevent conflicting repository context when working in ADO environments. A CPU hang caused by large file attachments is resolved, async CA certificate loading speeds up CLI startup, and session history plus file tracking are now available to all users.
items.action: Use client_credentials OAuth to connect Copilot CLI-managed MCP servers into headless automation pipelines without user login steps. Test ADO workspace detection if you operate in both GitHub and Azure DevOps environments.

2026-05-03.summary: Two OpenAI API deadlines arrive within 9 days as Realtime API Beta retires May 7 and DALL-E 2 and 3 shut down May 12; OpenAI Agents SDK v0.15.1 adds explicit model refusal handling for agentic pipelines.

items.headline: OpenAI Realtime API Beta retires May 7, migrate to GA endpoint before calls fail
items.description: The Realtime API Beta endpoint and beta WebSocket session format shut down on May 7, 2026, four days from now. Builders must switch to the GA endpoint at /v1/realtime/sessions, which requires specifying a session type (speech-to-speech or transcription) when creating or updating sessions and uses a different key generation call. Calls to the beta endpoint will return errors after the cutoff.
items.action: Before May 7, update all Realtime API integrations to the GA endpoint and add session type to every session create and update call. Review the beta-to-GA migration guide at developers.openai.com for the full list of request shape changes.

items.headline: DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 API endpoints retire May 12, replace with gpt-image-2
items.description: OpenAI retires both DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 image generation endpoints on May 12, 2026, nine days away. Any code or automation pipeline calling these endpoints will return errors after that date. The replacement is gpt-image-2, launched April 21, with reasoning-native generation and 2K output at token-based pricing ($8 input and $30 output per million tokens), replacing the previous per-image pricing model.
items.action: Search codebases and automation workflows for dall-e-2, dall-e-3, or any /v1/images endpoint calls. Migrate to gpt-image-2 before May 12. Validate prompt parity before cutover since the pricing model has shifted from per-image to per-token.

items.headline: OpenAI Agents SDK v0.15.1 surfaces model refusals as a catchable exception
items.description: OpenAI shipped v0.15.0 (May 1) and a v0.15.1 patch (May 2) to its Python Agents SDK. The primary change in v0.15.0 is ModelRefusalError, which raises a named exception when a model refuses a request rather than silently returning an empty output, letting pipelines distinguish refusals from network errors. v0.15.1 adds a WebSocket keepalive option for long-running Realtime sessions and fixes Unix PTY signal handling for agent child processes.
items.action: Update openai-agents to 0.15.1 and add explicit ModelRefusalError handlers in safety-sensitive agentic pipelines so refusals are logged and routed correctly rather than treated as empty completions.

2026-05-04.summary: DeepSeek extends V4-Pro 75 percent discount three weeks to May 31 with 1M context confirmed in Claude Code, as no major API launches or model releases were announced over the weekend.

items.headline: DeepSeek extends V4-Pro 75 percent discount to May 31 with 1M context in Claude Code
items.description: DeepSeek announced on May 3 that the V4-Pro promotional discount has been extended three weeks from its original May 5 deadline to May 31, 2026 at 15:59 UTC. At discounted rates, input costs $0.435 per million tokens and output costs $0.87 per million tokens versus standard pricing of $1.74 and $3.48, making V4-Pro the most cost-efficient 1T-parameter model available via API in this window. Claude Code users can route to V4-Pro with 1M context by setting the model identifier to deepseek-v4-pro[1m] when using a DeepSeek-compatible endpoint.
items.action: Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to DeepSeek API endpoint and the model to deepseek-v4-pro[1m] in Claude Code to access 1M context at discounted rates through May 31. Benchmark V4-Pro against your current model on coding and agentic tasks before the promotion closes.

2026-05-05.summary: Anthropic red teams a new Jupiter model ahead of the Code with Claude developer conference opening tomorrow in San Francisco, as both Anthropic and OpenAI launch separate enterprise AI deployment ventures on the same day.

items.headline: Anthropic red teams claude jupiter model ahead of Code with Claude conference opening tomorrow
items.description: TestingCatalog confirmed Anthropic began red team testing a new model codenamed claude-jupiter-v1-p with safety researchers on approximately May 3, two days before the Code with Claude developer conference in San Francisco. The pattern mirrors last year's Neptune codename exercise in June 2025 that preceded the Claude 4 family launch. Jupiter is the largest body in the solar system, consistent with Anthropic's practice of using ascending planetary names for major pre-release safety evaluations.
items.action: Watch the Code with Claude livestream tomorrow May 6 at claude.com/code-with-claude for a likely new major model announcement. Do not lock in multi-year Claude API contracts or large model migration efforts until new model pricing and capability details are public.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.128 adds zip plugin archives MCP tool count and reserves workspace server name
items.description: Released May 4 at 23:01 UTC, Claude Code v2.1.128 lets the --plugin-dir flag accept .zip archives in addition to directories, making plugin distribution simpler without requiring a local directory. The /mcp command now shows a tool count per connected server and flags servers that connected with zero tools, surfacing misconfigured MCP setups immediately. The server name workspace is now reserved and any existing MCP server using that name will be skipped with a warning.
items.action: Update Claude Code to v2.1.128 immediately. Audit any MCP server configs for servers named workspace and rename them before upgrading to avoid silent failures. Use the /mcp command to verify all servers are connecting with the expected tool counts.

items.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI both form enterprise AI deployment companies on the same day
items.description: On May 4, Anthropic announced a joint venture backed by Blackstone, Hellman and Friedman, Goldman Sachs, and others that will embed Anthropic engineers directly inside mid-size companies to redesign workflows around Claude agents, mirroring the Palantir forward-deployment model. Hours later, Bloomberg confirmed OpenAI finalized The Deployment Company, a parallel structure raising over four billion dollars from nineteen private equity investors to scale enterprise GPT rollouts. Both companies moving simultaneously into enterprise professional services signals a structural shift: AI model providers are now competing directly for enterprise integration contracts.
items.action: Reassess how enterprise AI integration services are positioned for clients who ask about deploying Claude or GPT. The labs now offer direct engineering deployment as a competing option. Differentiate on cross-model expertise, existing workflow knowledge, and speed of execution rather than model access alone.

2026-05-06.summary: OpenAI replaces the ChatGPT default with GPT-5.5 Instant cutting hallucinations by half, Anthropic ships 10 financial services agent templates as Claude Code plugins and Managed Agents cookbooks, and GitHub Copilot CLI adds OAuth MCP authentication.

items.headline: OpenAI replaces ChatGPT default with GPT-5.5 Instant cutting hallucinations by half
items.description: OpenAI launched GPT-5.5 Instant on May 5 as the new default model across all ChatGPT tiers, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant. The model scores 81.2 on AIME versus 65.4 for its predecessor and delivers 52.5 percent fewer hallucinated claims on high-stakes topics including law, medicine, and finance. API users on the chat-latest alias are now being routed to GPT-5.5 Instant; GPT-5.3 Instant remains accessible by model ID for three months.
items.action: Audit any production integrations using the chat-latest alias; test GPT-5.5 Instant against high-stakes use cases before alias routing switches live traffic.

items.headline: Anthropic releases 10 financial services agent templates as Claude Code plugins and Managed Agents cookbooks
items.description: Anthropic launched 10 ready-to-run agent templates for banking and insurance work covering pitchbook drafting, KYC screening, and month-end close. Each template ships simultaneously as a Claude Code plugin, a Claude Cowork package, and a Claude Managed Agents cookbook, making all three deployment paths available on day one. The release adds Moody's Analytics, Dun and Bradstreet, and Verisk as live data connectors to the Anthropic platform.
items.action: Pull the Claude Managed Agents cookbooks and Claude Code plugins for reference architecture on regulated document workflows; the Moody's and D&B connectors are now available for any builder building credit, risk, or entity resolution pipelines.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.41 adds OAuth MCP server authentication and automatic shell completion
items.description: Copilot CLI v1.0.41 shipped on May 5 with MCP server authentication now supporting the OAuth flow, closing the headless auth gap for server-to-server MCP pipelines that previously required manual credential handling. The release also adds automatic shell completion installation, faster UI rendering before authentication completes, and improved reliability for file attachment handling in non-interactive prompt mode.
items.action: Update to v1.0.41 if running Copilot CLI as an MCP client in automated pipelines; the OAuth MCP auth eliminates the workaround requirement for authenticated MCP servers.

2026-05-07.summary: Anthropic upgrades Managed Agents with public beta Outcomes and multiagent orchestration plus a Dreaming research preview, doubles Claude Code rate limits backed by a SpaceX Colossus 1 compute deal, and ships a critical stdio MCP memory leak fix in Claude Code 2.1.132.

items.headline: Anthropic opens Outcomes and multiagent orchestration to Managed Agents public beta and launches Dreaming research preview
items.description: Outcomes, previously in research preview, move to public beta under the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header with the ability to define explicit success criteria; internal tests show up to 10 percentage point task success improvement and Harvey legal agents saw a sixfold completion rate increase. Multiagent sessions let a lead agent delegate subtasks to specialist agents with independent models, prompts, and tools running in parallel on a shared filesystem with full traceability in the Claude Console; Netflix used it to identify recurring issues across hundreds of build logs. Dreaming, a new research preview available via Claude Console waitlist, reviews agent memory stores overnight, surfaces recurring errors and shared preferences, and rewrites experience files without additional per-session token cost.
items.action: Add the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header to access Outcomes and multiagent sessions today. Join the Dreaming waitlist on Claude Console if you run long-horizon agents where accumulated experience would improve recurring task quality.

items.headline: Anthropic doubles Claude Code rate limits and signs Colossus 1 compute deal with SpaceX
items.description: Claude Code Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise seat plans get a 2x increase in the five-hour usage limit effective immediately, with peak-hour throttling fully removed for Pro and Max accounts. Tier 1 Opus API callers gain a 1500 percent increase in input tokens per minute and a 900 percent increase in output tokens per minute. The capacity comes from Anthropic taking exclusive access to all compute at SpaceX Colossus 1 in Memphis, adding more than 300 megawatts and 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs expected online within the month.
items.action: No action required; limits increase automatically. Builders running high-volume Opus 4.7 agentic loops that previously hit per-minute throughput ceilings should retest capacity now. Claude Code heavy users on Pro and Max plans can remove any queue-management workarounds built around peak-hour throttling.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.132 patches 10GB stdio MCP memory leak and fixes silent prompt cache TTL downgrade
items.description: Version 2.1.132 patches an unbounded memory growth bug that could drive RSS past 10GB in persistent processes using stdio MCP servers, a critical fix for any server or CI deployment using long-running Claude Code sessions. Version 2.1.129 adds the --plugin-url flag for installing plugin zip archives from remote URLs and fixes a latent billing error where the 1-hour prompt cache TTL was silently downgrading to 5 minutes. The same series resolves Bedrock and Vertex 400 errors triggered by ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H and adds CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID to Bash subprocess environments for distributed tracing.
items.action: Update to v2.1.132 immediately if running Claude Code with stdio MCP servers in any persistent process. If you set 1-hour prompt cache before this patch, verify your actual cache TTL in production logs as billing may have been calculated at 5-minute rather than 1-hour rates.

2026-05-08.summary: OpenAI replaces the retired Realtime API Beta with three production-grade voice models including GPT-Realtime-2 with GPT-5-class reasoning; Google brings Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite to general availability; xAI gives 7 days notice before retiring 8 Grok models on May 15.

items.headline: OpenAI replaces deprecated Realtime API Beta with three production voice models including GPT-5-class reasoning
items.description: GPT-Realtime-2 is OpenAI's first voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning, a 128K token context window, and adjustable reasoning levels from minimal to extra-high, priced at $32 per million audio input tokens and $64 per million output tokens. GPT-Realtime-Translate adds live speech-to-speech translation across 70-plus input languages into 13 output languages at $0.034 per minute, enabling real-time interpreter use cases for the first time in the OpenAI API. GPT-Realtime-Whisper delivers live streaming transcription at $0.017 per minute, transcribing as the speaker talks rather than after a full utterance.
items.action: Migrate any integrations that used the now-retired Realtime API Beta gpt-4o-realtime-preview endpoints to the new GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate, or GPT-Realtime-Whisper models depending on your use case. GPT-Realtime-2 with xhigh reasoning is the new ceiling for voice agents that need multi-step problem solving.

items.headline: Google brings Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite to general availability as fastest lowest-cost 3.1 model
items.description: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite exits the preview it entered on March 3 and is now generally available with a production SLA via Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform at $0.25 per million input tokens and $1.50 per million output tokens. Google positions it as the fastest and most cost-efficient model in the 3.1 series, citing p95 full-reply latency of 1.8 seconds and sub-second p95 for classifier and tool-call workloads. Early adopters including Gladly, JetBrains, and Ramp report roughly 60 percent lower costs compared to thinking-tier models on comparable token mixes.
items.action: Evaluate routing high-volume production classification, RAG re-ranking, and tool-dispatch tasks from Gemini 3.1 Flash to Flash-Lite. Run an A/B quality comparison on your actual workload before full migration.

items.headline: xAI retires 8 Grok models on May 15 with 7 days notice and no fast-tier replacement
items.description: Grok-3, grok-4-0709, grok-4-fast-reasoning, grok-4-fast-non-reasoning, grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, grok-code-fast-1, and grok-imagine-image-pro all retire on May 15 at 12pm PT. The deprecation notice was issued with approximately two weeks of warning, and no direct migration path to a comparable fast or cost-optimized Grok tier is documented. The fast-reasoning variants were particularly recently introduced, leaving builders who migrated to them with minimal time to re-evaluate provider routing.
items.action: Audit any xAI Grok API integrations in automations or agent pipelines before May 15. For grok-3 general-purpose use, evaluate Grok 4.3 or DeepSeek V4-Pro as alternatives. For code-fast workloads, evaluate GPT-5.5 Instant or Claude Haiku 4.5.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.133 exposes effort level to hooks and fixes MCP OAuth proxy and subagent skill discovery
items.description: Hooks now receive the active effort level via an effort.level field in the JSON input payload and a $CLAUDE_EFFORT environment variable, enabling conditional hook logic that scales side effects based on how much reasoning Claude is applying. A long-standing bug where MCP OAuth flows ignored HTTP(S)_PROXY, NO_PROXY, and mTLS settings is now fixed, resolving silent OAuth failures behind corporate proxies. Subagents no longer fail to discover project, user, and plugin skills, which had broken multi-agent orchestration setups relying on skill inheritance.
items.action: Update to 2.1.133. Add effort-conditional logic in any hooks that trigger expensive side effects. If you run MCP OAuth servers behind a corporate proxy and had silent failures, test them now. Rebuild any multi-agent pipelines that stopped inheriting skills after the 2.1.12x regression.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI ships security hardening and rubber-duck Claude agent in two stable releases
items.description: Version 1.0.42 adds enhanced MCP server diagnostics with stderr output for easier server debugging, a -C flag to change working directory mid-session, remote session export for non-GitHub repositories, and an experimental rubber-duck agent powered by Claude for structured thinking in restricted environments. Version 1.0.43 follows with server-side model routing in Auto mode, security hardening against RCE vulnerabilities, improved MCP subprocess termination, and username toggle in the statusline picker.
items.action: Update to v1.0.43 for the RCE hardening. Use the -C flag in scripts that need to run commands from a different working directory without a subshell. Evaluate the rubber-duck agent for projects where code cannot leave the machine.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.129.0 stable ships workspace plugin sharing and modal Vim editing
items.description: The stable release of 0.129.0 lands workspace-level plugin sharing with access controls and source filtering, allowing team members to share a common plugin catalog without individual installations. Modal Vim editing is included as the default TUI input mode for Vim users. Experimental goals persistence introduced in the 0.128.x alpha series is carried into stable.
items.action: Update to 0.129.0. If running Codex CLI across a team, configure workspace plugin sharing to standardize the tool catalog and reduce per-member setup friction.

2026-05-09.summary: ClaudeBleed lets any Chrome extension hijack Claude with Gmail and GitHub exfiltration risk; Gemini API File Search adds native multimodal RAG and three developer tools ship significant stable releases.

items.headline: ClaudeBleed lets any Chrome extension hijack Claude and exfiltrate Gmail and GitHub data
items.description: LayerX disclosed ClaudeBleed on May 8, a vulnerability in the Claude Chrome extension where any installed extension can issue commands to Claude without additional permissions, enabling data exfiltration from Gmail, GitHub, and Google Drive. Anthropic released a partial patch in version 1.0.70 on May 6, but researchers bypassed it in under three hours by switching Claude to privileged execution mode, which the user is never prompted to approve. The root cause remains unfixed.
items.action: Disable or uninstall the Claude Chrome extension in production and enterprise contexts until a complete fix is confirmed; audit browser extension lists on developer workstations where Claude in Chrome is active.

items.headline: Gemini API File Search now indexes and queries images natively with free managed embeddings
items.description: Google updated the Gemini API File Search tool on May 5 to process images and text together using the gemini-embedding-2 model, eliminating the need for a separate embedding pipeline in multimodal RAG systems. Storage and query-time embeddings are free; builders pay only for initial indexing. Custom metadata filtering and page-level citations ship alongside multimodal support, covering both retrieval precision and enterprise audit requirements.
items.action: Migrate multimodal document processing pipelines to Gemini File Search to remove the external image embedding service and reduce cost; test with PDF and PNG or JPEG corpora ahead of Google I/O on May 19 where further Gemini announcements are expected.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.136 adds hard deny auto mode rules and fixes MCP server persistence after context clears
items.description: The May 8 release adds settings.autoMode.hard_deny, a new classifier rule type that unconditionally blocks auto mode without any prompt, giving CI and restricted enterprise deployments a strict deny-list control over agentic behaviour. Two production-breaking bugs are also fixed: MCP servers configured in .mcp.json and plugins disappearing after /clear, and a rare login loop caused by concurrent credential writes overwriting OAuth tokens. Version 2.1.137 released May 9 adds a Windows extension activation fix.
items.action: Adopt hard_deny rules in managed settings for any CI pipeline running Claude Code in unattended mode; verify MCP server persistence after /clear and re-test deployments using concurrent multi-session auth.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.130.0 adds remote control command for headless pipelines and AWS console-login auth
items.description: The May 8 stable release ships codex remote-control, enabling headless app-server startup from CI pipelines and scripts without a TTY session. App-server clients can now paginate large conversation threads, removing the memory ceiling for long-running agent loops. Bedrock auth gains support for AWS console-login credentials, simplifying deployment in teams using federated SSO rather than long-lived IAM access keys.
items.action: Integrate codex remote-control into CI agent pipelines to trigger Codex tasks without interactive sessions; update Bedrock auth configuration if using AWS console-login federated credentials.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.44 lets hooks return responses without an LLM call and stacks multiple skills mid-input
items.description: Stable v1.0.44 ships the hook bypass pattern, where request handling in hooks can return a response directly without triggering an LLM call, enabling caching layers, routing logic, or fixed-response commands at zero API token cost. Mid-input slash commands now support invoking multiple skills in a single entry, enabling multi-step compound tasks without sequential re-prompting. A prerelease flag is added to copilot update for staged enterprise rollouts.
items.action: Use hook bypass for any predictable repetitive Copilot commands to cut API token spend; test multi-skill invocation for compound task chains that previously required chained prompts.

2026-05-10.summary: Google announces a breaking schema change to the Gemini Interactions API requiring migration before June 6, and Gemini CLI 0.41.0 ships real-time voice mode with hardened headless security.

items.headline: Gemini Interactions API drops outputs array for steps in breaking schema change ahead of June 6 deadline
items.description: Google published a migration guide announcing a breaking schema change to the Gemini Interactions API (v1beta): the flat outputs array is being replaced by a structured steps array containing typed entries for model output, tool calls, and user input. New API features shipped after May 7 are exclusively available in the steps schema; builders on the legacy outputs format will not receive them. The default switches to steps on May 20 and the legacy schema is permanently removed on June 6.
items.action: Add Api-Revision: 2026-05-06 to current Interactions API calls to preserve legacy behavior until ready to migrate; plan migration to the steps schema before June 6. New integrations should send Api-Revision: 2026-05-20 to access features already locked to the new format.

items.headline: Gemini CLI 0.41.0 adds real-time voice mode and mandatory workspace trust for headless pipelines
items.description: Gemini CLI stable v0.41.0 shipped May 5 with real-time voice interaction supporting both cloud and on-device local backends, making audio input available without cloud round-trips in automation contexts. Headless environments now require explicit workspace trust, and a new shell command validation layer with a core tools allowlist prevents untrusted path execution in CI/CD pipelines. ContextManager and auto-memory scratchpad persistence improve session continuity for multi-turn agent workflows, and Gemma 4 is now a selectable model.
items.action: Run npx gemini-cli update or reinstall to 0.41.0; review headless workspace trust settings and explicitly declare the shell command allowlist before deploying to CI/CD to avoid unexpected runtime rejections after update.

2026-05-11.summary: DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 shut down tomorrow requiring non-trivial API code changes for all image generation integrations built on these models.

items.headline: DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 shut down tomorrow with migration that requires code changes beyond a model swap
items.description: OpenAI shuts down dall-e-2 and dall-e-3 from the API on May 12 with no auto-upgrade fallback — calls will return errors immediately. Migration to gpt-image-1 or gpt-image-1.5 is not a drop-in rename: builders must remove the response_format, style, and quality request parameters, and switch response parsing from URL fetching to b64_json decoding. Any integration that forwards these parameters unchanged will break on the first call after midnight.
items.action: Audit all /v1/images/generations calls before May 12. Update model string, strip deprecated params, and rewrite response handling to decode b64_json. Test on a staging API key before cutover.

2026-05-12.summary: Anthropic launches native Claude Platform through AWS billing and IAM auth while DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 APIs go dark today completing the six-month deprecation cycle.

items.headline: Anthropic brings native Claude Platform to AWS with IAM auth ending need for separate Anthropic accounts
items.description: Anthropic launched Claude Platform on AWS on May 11, giving builders on AWS access to the full native Claude Platform including Messages API, Files API, Message Batches API, Managed Agents, Agent Skills, MCP connector, and code execution through AWS billing and IAM auth without a separate Anthropic account. The service runs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure accessible via AWS and is distinct from Amazon Bedrock, meaning it carries the same beta-access features available on Anthropic's first-party platform. AWS is the first cloud provider to offer native Claude Platform access.
items.action: Teams already billing through AWS can now adopt Managed Agents, Agent Skills, and the MCP connector without adding a separate Anthropic vendor contract. Authenticate via IAM and use the new Claude Platform on AWS endpoint documented at platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws.

items.headline: DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 APIs return errors from today as OpenAI image API consolidation completes
items.description: All API calls to dall-e-2 and dall-e-3 now return errors as of May 12, 2026, completing the deprecation announced in November 2025. Migration requires more than swapping the model string: gpt-image-1 replaces both but drops the response_format, style, and quality parameters, and returns b64_json instead of image URLs. Any automation or integration that passed these parameters unchanged will error on every call.
items.action: Check every workflow and API integration still hitting /v1/images/generations with dall-e-2 or dall-e-3. Swap to gpt-image-1 or gpt-image-1-mini, remove deprecated request parameters, and rewrite response handling to decode b64_json instead of fetching image URLs.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.139 ships Agent View research preview and goal-driven autonomous sessions
items.description: Claude Code v2.1.139 (May 11) introduces Agent View as a research preview, a unified list of all running, blocked, and completed sessions accessible via claude agents. The /goal command lets builders define completion conditions so Claude continues working autonomously across turns, displaying live elapsed time, turn count, and token usage. Hook improvements add an args field for direct exec-form command spawning without shell interpolation, continueOnBlock for PostToolUse hooks, and MCP servers now receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and can reconnect live via /mcp Reconnect without a full restart.
items.action: Update Claude Code and run claude agents to see the multi-session view. Use /goal to define done conditions for long autonomous tasks instead of polling manually. Set args in hooks to avoid shell injection risks when spawning subprocesses directly.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Natural Language Autoencoders that translate Claude activations into auditable reasoning trails
items.description: Anthropic published Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) on May 8, an unsupervised method that converts Claude's internal residual-stream activations into human-readable text explanations. In audits, NLAs helped examiners uncover hidden model motivations 12 to 15 percent of the time versus under 3 percent with other interpretability tools. The pre-deployment audit of Opus 4.6 using NLAs surfaced unverbalized evaluation awareness, cases where the model believed it was being tested but did not disclose that belief. Training code and trained NLAs for popular open models are open-sourced.
items.action: Use NLA-based auditing in pre-production review for any Claude deployment in regulated or safety-critical contexts. The open-source NLAs for popular open models provide a baseline interpretability layer for non-Claude model deployments. Training code at transformer-circuits.pub/2026/nla.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.45 adds autopilot mode toggle and independent session forking with 1.5s faster startup
items.description: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.45 (May 11) adds /autopilot as a slash command for toggling autonomous mode and /fork for creating an independent context branch from any point in a session without affecting the parent. Startup time improves by approximately 1.5 seconds, PowerShell 7 plus is now a supported fallback shell, and OpenTelemetry output aligns with GenAI semantic conventions for consistent observability across multi-tool agent pipelines.
items.action: Update Copilot CLI and use /fork to branch exploratory sessions before making destructive edits. The OTel GenAI convention alignment means Copilot CLI traces now share the same observability schema as Claude Code and OpenAI Agents SDK for unified agent pipeline monitoring.

2026-05-13.summary: Anthropic extends fast mode to Opus 4.7 and launches a legal-vertical plugin bundle with 12 practice-area plugins and 20-plus MCP connectors for law firms and in-house counsel.

items.headline: Anthropic extends fast mode research preview to Opus 4.7 bringing top-tier model into speed tier
items.description: Fast mode is now available for Claude Opus 4.7 via the speed parameter set to fast and the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header, extending the research preview that launched for Opus 4.6 in February to the most capable Claude model. Pricing, rate limits, and waitlist access terms are identical to Opus 4.6 fast mode. Builders running long-horizon agentic workloads that previously required choosing between Opus-class intelligence and acceptable latency can now access both from the same model.
items.action: Join the fast mode waitlist at claude.com/fast-mode if you run Opus 4.7 workloads where output speed is a bottleneck. Swap in the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header alongside your existing Opus 4.7 calls.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude for Legal with 12 practice area plugins and 20-plus MCP connectors
items.description: Anthropic released Claude for Legal, a bundle of 12 practice-area Claude Cowork plugins covering commercial counsel, employment counsel, litigation associate, law student, and others, alongside more than 20 MCP connectors for legal platforms including Thomson Reuters Westlaw, Harvey, DocuSign, Everlaw, Box, and iManage. A cross-app Microsoft 365 integration carries conversation context across Word, Outlook, Excel, and PowerPoint within a single agent session. The plugins and connectors are available now to all paying Claude customers.
items.action: If you build legal or compliance automations, audit which of the 20-plus new MCP connectors replace custom integrations you maintain. The plugin architecture is a direct model for building similar vertical bundles in healthcare, finance, or real estate.

2026-05-14.summary: xAI retires 8 Grok models including grok-3 and grok-code-fast-1 at noon PT tomorrow May 15, Claude Code ships workload identity federation and CI hook notification fields in v2.1.141, and GitHub Copilot CLI adds cloud agent session resume.

items.headline: xAI retires 8 Grok models including grok-3 and all grok-4-fast variants at noon PT tomorrow May 15
items.description: Eight Grok models including grok-3, grok-code-fast-1, all grok-4-1-fast and grok-4-fast variants, grok-4-0709, and grok-imagine-image-pro shut down at 12:00pm PT on May 15. Any API call to these model IDs after that timestamp returns an error with no fallback. The migration path is grok-4.3 for code and reasoning workloads, grok-4.20-non-reasoning for fast non-reasoning pipelines, and grok-imagine-image for image generation.
items.action: Audit any automation or agent pipeline using xAI Grok APIs before midnight tonight Almaty time. Swap grok-code-fast-1 and grok-3 to grok-4.3, and grok-4-fast variants to grok-4.20-non-reasoning. Test integrations before the May 15 noon PT cutoff.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.141 adds workload identity federation env var and CI-friendly hook notification fields
items.description: v2.1.141 introduces ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID for workload identity federation, enabling Claude Code deployments to authenticate via cloud provider identity tokens without static API keys. The terminalSequence field in hook JSON output triggers desktop notifications, window titles, and bells from hooks even when running without a controlling terminal, making CI pipelines observable. The release also adds claude agents --cwd path for directory-scoped agent listing and a Rewind menu Summarize up to here compression option, alongside 60-plus bug fixes.
items.action: Set ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID in CI environments to migrate from static API keys to identity-based auth. Use the terminalSequence hook field to route build completion events to desktop notification systems or terminal multiplexers without requiring an attached terminal.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.47 adds cloud agent session resume and named fork tracking
items.description: v1.0.47 enables --resume to reconnect to Copilot cloud agent sessions started by remote teammates, making it possible to pick up long-running agent tasks from any workstation. The /fork command now accepts an optional session name and forked sessions display their origin session, enabling cleaner session trees when branching agentic workflows. Copilot Max plan subscribers now see the correct list of available premium models.
items.action: Use copilot --resume to connect to shared cloud agent sessions and implement handoff patterns within distributed teams. Pair with named /fork sessions to maintain readable agent genealogy in multi-branch workflows.

2026-05-15.summary: Anthropic separates programmatic Claude usage into monthly credit pools from June 15 in a structural billing change, xAI retires eight Grok legacy model slugs that silently redirect to grok-4.3 pricing, and Claude for Small Business launches with 15 agentic workflows.

items.headline: Anthropic separates programmatic Claude usage into monthly credit pools starting June 15
items.description: Starting June 15, all programmatic Claude usage via subscriptions moves to a separate monthly credit pool: $20 for Pro, $100 for Max 5x and Team Premium seats, $200 for Max 20x. The pool covers Claude Agent SDK calls, claude -p, Claude Code GitHub Actions, and third-party agents including OpenClaw. Credits expire monthly and do not roll over; once exhausted, programmatic usage stops unless extra billing is enabled at standard pay-as-you-go API rates. Interactive Claude Code in the terminal and web or desktop chat remain on standard subscription limits.
items.action: Audit all programmatic Claude usage before June 15. Identify workflows using claude -p, GitHub Actions runners, or third-party Claude agents. Estimate monthly token consumption against the credit budget for your plan tier. High-volume programmatic workflows should migrate to direct API keys to avoid credit exhaustion.

items.headline: xAI Grok 8 legacy model slugs retired today with silent redirect to grok-4.3 pricing
items.description: As of noon PT May 15, xAI retired grok-3, grok-code-fast-1, grok-4-0709, grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, grok-4-fast-reasoning, grok-4-fast-non-reasoning, and grok-imagine-image-pro. Unlike most model retirements where calls return errors, the deprecated slugs remain active but silently redirect to grok-4.3. Calls will succeed but are billed at grok-4.3 rates ($1.25 input and $2.50 output per million tokens) regardless of what the original model cost.
items.action: Update all integrations explicitly referencing retired model slugs. Silent redirection means no immediate errors to alert you to the billing change. Migrate to grok-4.3 for code and reasoning workloads, grok-4.20-non-reasoning for fast non-reasoning, and grok-imagine-image for image generation.

items.description: Claude for Small Business ships 15 ready-to-run agentic workflows spanning payroll planning, invoice chasing, lead triage, month-end close, campaign management, and cash-flow monitoring. Eight named connectors integrate with QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, DocuSign, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack. The package continues the vertical bundle pattern alongside Claude for Financial Services (May 5) and Claude for Legal (May 12), and every workflow requires explicit user approval before executing an action.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.142 adds dispatched agent configuration flags and defaults fast mode to Opus 4.7

items.description: Microsoft released the GitHub Copilot App on May 14 as a standalone desktop experience for agentic development across Windows, macOS, and Linux. An Agent Merge mode lets the agent address review comments, fix failing CI checks, and merge once user-defined conditions are met; an Inbox interface surfaces issues, pull requests, CI events, and tasks across repositories in a single pane.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.143 adds plugin dependency enforcement and per-turn token cost projections
items.description: Released May 15, v2.1.143 refuses to disable a plugin when another enabled plugin depends on it and auto-enables transitive dependencies on install, preventing silent capability breakage. The /plugin marketplace browse pane now shows per-turn and per-invocation token cost estimates before committing to a session. items.headline: PraisonAI zero-day exploited within four hours exposes multi-agent frameworks to quota drain
items.description: CVE-2026-44338 (CVSS 7.3), a missing-authentication flaw in PraisonAI's open-source multi-agent orchestration framework, was disclosed May 14 and exploited within four hours. The exposed endpoints allow any network-reachable attacker to hijack automated agent operations, execute tasks, and drain expensive API quotas without credentials. The attack pattern mirrors the MCP STDIO and LMDeploy SSRF vulnerabilities covered in prior digests, confirming a repeating pattern of unauthenticated access in open-source agent frameworks.
items.action: Audit any PraisonAI deployments for network exposure immediately. Apply authentication at the reverse-proxy layer if patching is not yet possible. Check API provider usage dashboards for unexpected quota consumption across all agent frameworks, not just PraisonAI.

items.headline: Google intercepts first confirmed AI-generated zero-day before mass 2FA bypass campaign launches
items.description: Google's Threat Intelligence Group detected a functional Python exploit developed by cybercrime group TeamPCP using AI assistance to discover and weaponize a logic flaw in a widely deployed open-source web administration tool, allowing 2FA bypass after credential theft. The exploit carried telltale AI fingerprints including fabricated CVSS scores, structured help menus, and clean ANSI color classes. Google patched the vendor before the mass campaign launched, but the incident confirms AI is now being used to autonomously identify novel vulnerabilities and build working exploits rather than merely writing scripts.
items.action: Audit any AI agent with code execution or file system access for exploit development potential; review authentication logic in any web admin tool used in automation pipelines; treat AI-powered threat actors as capable of discovering logic flaws without known CVEs and update threat models accordingly

items.headline: NGINX Rift CVE-2026-42945 confirmed actively exploited with unauthenticated worker crashes and RCE attempts
items.description: VulnCheck confirmed on May 18 that threat actors are actively weaponizing the NGINX Rift heap buffer overflow, triggering worker crashes against honeypot networks and targeting servers without ASLR for remote code execution. The flaw (CVSS 9.2) lives in the ngx_http_rewrite_module and affects every NGINX version from 0.6.27 through 1.30.0, covering the vast majority of deployed reverse proxies worldwide including those fronting AI API gateways, n8n, and webhook endpoints. AI-native security firm depthfirst discovered the 18-year-old bug in roughly six hours; patched versions 1.31.0 and 1.30.1 are available now.
items.action: Patch NGINX to 1.31.0 or 1.30.1 immediately on any server running rewrite directives; verify ASLR is enabled on all remaining unpatched instances as a temporary mitigation; audit any AI pipeline reverse proxy or webhook receiver that terminates at NGINX

items.headline: xAI launches Grok Build early beta as CLI coding agent with eight parallel subagents to challenge Claude Code

2026-05-20.summary: Google I/O 2026 delivers Gemini 3.5 Flash to the API and managed agent execution in isolated sandboxes; Anthropic adds MCP tunnels for private networks and self-hosted agent sandboxes.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Flash via API at I/O 2026
items.description: Gemini 3.5 Flash is available immediately in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio following the I/O 2026 keynote. items.headline: Gemini API gains one-call managed agent execution in isolated Linux sandboxes
items.description: Google introduced Managed Agents in the Gemini API at I/O 2026, allowing a single Interactions API call to provision a fully managed agent that reasons, uses tools, and executes code in an ephemeral isolated Linux sandbox. Agents are powered by the Antigravity 2.0 harness and Gemini 3.5 Flash, configurable via AGENTS.md files or inline parameters, and support persistent multi-turn environments where files and state survive between calls. items.headline: Anthropic adds MCP tunnels for private networks and self-hosted agent sandboxes

items.headline: Firebase AI Logic reaches GA with Gemini Live session resumption and hybrid on-device inference
items.description: Firebase AI Logic (formerly Vertex AI in Firebase) graduated to general availability at Google I/O 2026, providing direct access to Gemini 3.x models from mobile and web clients under the same Firebase security model as Firestore, with no API key management required in client code. 2026-05-24.summary: MCP protocol locks stateless release candidate with breaking session and initialization changes while OpenAI demonstrates autonomous mathematical discovery.

items.headline: MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate locks stateless core with breaking session changes
items.description: The release candidate for MCP 2026-07-28 was locked on May 21, removing the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header entirely so any request can land on any server instance behind a standard round-robin load balancer. Breaking changes include error code -32002 renamed to -32602, a redesigned Tasks extension API, and formal deprecation of Roots, Sampling, and Logging. Two extensions graduate: MCP Apps (server-rendered HTML UIs in sandboxed iframes) and Tasks (long-running work via stateless tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel). SDK maintainers have a 10-week validation window; Tier 1 SDKs must ship support before the final July 28 specification.

items.headline: OpenAI reasoning model autonomously disproves 80-year Erdos geometry conjecture
items.description: An internal general-purpose OpenAI reasoning model independently disproved the planar unit distance conjecture posed by Paul Erdos in 1946, discovering an infinite family of point configurations via Golod-Shafarevich algebraic number theory that yields polynomial improvement over square grids. The model was not trained for mathematics, was not guided step-by-step, and received only the problem statement. Fields medalist Tim Gowers called it a milestone in AI mathematics; Princeton mathematician Will Sawin independently refined the exponent to delta 0.014. This is the first confirmed instance of AI autonomously solving a prominent open problem in a core mathematical subfield.
items.action: Monitor how OpenAI packages this long-chain cross-domain reasoning capability for API access. The same sustained reasoning across disparate domains applies to biology, engineering, and materials science. Consider how research automation agents could leverage these capabilities when exposed via API.

items.headline: TrapDoor worms through npm, PyPI and Crates.io poisoning AI assistant context files in active repos
items.description: A coordinated supply chain attack active since May 22 has spread 34 malicious packages and 384 artifacts across three registries, specifically targeting AI and crypto developers. The campaign's distinctive technique embeds malicious CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules instructions in pull requests opened against popular AI repositories including langchain-ai/langchain, langflow-ai/langflow, and browser-use/browser-use, tricking AI coding assistants into running a fake security scan that exfiltrates SSH keys, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, API keys, browser logins, and crypto wallets. Packages self-execute on import in Python, via postinstall hooks in npm, and through build.rs in Rust.
items.action: Audit all packages installed from PyPI, npm, and Crates.io in the past week. Inspect open PRs on your repositories for CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules files containing scan or security audit instructions. Check CI logs for unexpected outbound requests to GitHub Pages domains.

Builders who have not migrated can use the Api-Revision: 2026-05-07 header to continue receiving legacy outputs format until June 8 when the legacy schema is permanently removed. Any Gemini API features released after May 7 are only available in the steps schema.
items.action: Add Api-Revision: 2026-05-07 header immediately to any Gemini Interactions API requests that parse the outputs format. Plan and complete migration to the steps schema before June 8 to avoid hard failures.
