items.headline: Malicious npm package mouse5212-super-formatter steals files from Claude user directory via GitHub exfiltration
items.description: The npm package mouse5212-super-formatter, uploaded May 26 as part of a campaign named Malware-Slop, targets the /mnt/user-data directory used by the Claude AI tool to handle uploads and outputs. During postinstall it authenticates to GitHub using either an environment-resident token or a hard-coded fallback, then synchronises local workspace files into an attacker-controlled repository. The package received 676 downloads and remains live on the npm registry. The threat actor shows signs of using AI to generate the malware code itself, citing verbose error handling, descriptive naming, and modular structure atypical for simple infostealers.
items.action: Run npm audit across all projects that install packages in environments where Claude Code or Claude Desktop is active. Check for mouse5212-super-formatter in node_modules and package-lock.json. Restrict GitHub token scopes in developer CI environments and rotate any tokens that exist in process.env on shared machines.

2026-05-29.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8 at the same price as Opus 4.7 with mid-conversation system messages, adaptive thinking and dynamic workflows capped at 1,000 subagents, while Codex CLI 0.135.0 adds named permission profiles for teams.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8 with mid-conversation system messages, adaptive thinking and dynamic workflows at same Opus 4.7 price
items.description: Claude Opus 4.8 ships at $5/$25 per MTok with a 1M token context window by default and 128k max output, same pricing as Opus 4.7. Two new API primitives launch alongside: mid-conversation system messages let harnesses update instructions mid-run while preserving the prompt cache, and refusal categories in stop_details let applications route different refusal types to the right fallback. Adaptive thinking triggers reasoning only when a turn needs it, spending similar tokens to Opus 4.7 at the same effort level with measurably better results; setting temperature, top_p, or top_k to non-default values now returns a 400 error, the same breaking change as Opus 4.7. Fast mode for Opus 4.8 is a research preview on the Claude API at 2x rate for 2.5x speed; fast mode for Opus 4.6 is deprecated with removal approximately 30 days after launch. Anthropic also confirmed Mythos-class models will reach all customers in the coming weeks.
items.action: Drop-in upgrade: swap claude-opus-4-7 for claude-opus-4-8 at same cost. Add mid-conversation system messages for agentic runs that need instruction pivots without cache invalidation. Verify your harness does not pass non-default temperature, top_p, or top_k or add the migration check before rollout. Migrate off Opus 4.6 fast mode before late June.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.154 ships dynamic workflows research preview with up to 1000 subagents per run and background shell commands
items.description: Claude Code 2.1.154 pairs with the Opus 4.8 launch to introduce dynamic workflows, where Claude writes a JavaScript orchestration script from your task description and a runtime executes it across up to 16 concurrent and 1,000 total subagents per session. Verified results from parallel agents are aggregated before they reach you, and active runs are tracked via the new /workflows command. Background shell commands now run with the ! shorthand without blocking the main session, and the computer use browser picker lets you target a specific connected browser via /chrome. The lean system prompt is now the default for all models except Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus 4.7 and earlier, trimming overhead on long agentic runs.
items.action: Upgrade Claude Code to 2.1.154. Describe a large codebase or data task and let Claude generate a workflow; use /workflows to monitor. The ! shortcut replaces the need to open a separate terminal for background jobs. Lean system prompt as default means token counts will drop for Opus 4.8 sessions.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.135.0 adds named permission profiles and text-object Vim editing for shared team configurations
items.description: Codex CLI 0.135.0 stable release adds named permission profiles to the /permissions command, letting teams define and share approval rulesets without respecifying them per session. Vim mode gains text-object editing and configurable keybindings, and codex doctor now reports richer environment and Git diagnostics for faster debug sessions.
items.action: Define named permission profiles for your team's standard Codex CLI access patterns and commit them to your project config. Teams running multiple developers on shared Codex sessions will benefit most from the shared ruleset approach.

2026-05-30.summary: Anthropic extends the full Managed Agents stack to Claude Platform on AWS while OpenAI opens free GPT-Rosalind API to vetted biodefense developers and publishes its first public governance framework aligned with EU and California AI law.

items.headline: Anthropic brings full Managed Agents stack to Claude Platform on AWS with webhooks, multiagent orchestration and self-hosted sandboxes
items.description: Builders using Claude Platform on AWS can now access the complete Managed Agents feature set: webhook notifications for session and vault lifecycle events, multiagent orchestration for parallel agent workloads, and self-hosted sandboxes that move tool execution onto their own AWS infrastructure while keeping orchestration on Anthropic. The new AnthropicSelfHostedEnvironmentAccess managed IAM policy gives AWS teams granular access control without requiring separate Anthropic credentials. This closes the parity gap between the direct Claude API and the AWS-hosted platform that existed since Claude Platform on AWS launched May 11.
items.action: Attach the AnthropicSelfHostedEnvironmentAccess managed policy to the IAM principal your agent worker runs as; configure webhook endpoints for session lifecycle monitoring in production pipelines.

items.headline: OpenAI opens free GPT-Rosalind API to vetted developers building pandemic preparedness and biodefense tools
items.description: The Rosalind Biodefense Program grants free GPT-Rosalind API access to academic, nonprofit, and mission-driven teams working on biosurveillance, epidemiological modeling, vaccine research, and non-pharmaceutical interventions. Partners Lawrence Livermore, Johns Hopkins APL, and CEPI are already using the model to advance protein engineering and pandemic preparedness. This is the third domain-restricted model access program this year after Claude Mythos for cybersecurity and GPT-5.4-Cyber for cyber defense, establishing gated access to specialized models as a standard pattern for high-stakes AI work.
items.action: Apply via openai.com/form/rosalind-biodefense-program if building AI tooling for public health, biosurveillance, or pandemic preparedness; note the program is U.S.-government-aligned with select international partners.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.157 auto-loads plugins from local skills directories and adds plugin scaffolding command
items.description: Plugins placed in any `.claude/skills` directory now load automatically without requiring marketplace installation, letting teams distribute custom capabilities entirely within their own codebase. The new `claude plugin init <name>` command scaffolds a plugin structure in the local skills directory, and tab-autocomplete now surfaces installed plugin names and available subcommands inline. Dispatched agent sessions now also honor the `agent` field in `settings.json`, enabling per-project agent defaults for multi-repo workflows.
items.action: Move team plugins to `.claude/skills` to eliminate the marketplace dependency; run `claude plugin init <name>` to scaffold new plugins from the terminal.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI ships Opus 4.8 support and per MCP server token usage metrics across two rapid releases
items.description: v1.0.55 (May 28) adds Claude Opus 4.8 as a supported model, reasoning token reporting that separates thinking tokens from output tokens, and per-MCP-server token usage metrics for multi-server deployments; the cell-based terminal renderer also switches to default for all users. v1.0.56 (May 29) extends model selection to free and student accounts, introduces a continuous-scroll diff view with sticky file and hunk headers, and adds atomic config file writes to prevent data loss during concurrent process updates.
items.action: Teams tracking LLM spend across multiple MCP servers should update to v1.0.55+ to get per-server token breakdowns; verify atomic config writes resolve any settings corruption seen in concurrent CI environments.

items.headline: OpenAI publishes Frontier Governance Framework mapping safety risk tiers to EU AI Act and California transparency law
items.description: The Frontier Governance Framework is OpenAI's first public document translating its internal Preparedness Framework into compliance language for specific regulatory obligations under the EU AI Act Code of Practice for General Purpose AI and California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act. Risk categories cover cyber offense, CBRN threats, harmful manipulation, and loss of control, each with defined assessment, mitigation, and reporting procedures. This establishes a public baseline for how frontier AI providers are expected to document and operationalize safety practices under emerging law.
items.action: EU and California-facing operators building on OpenAI should review the risk category definitions to align their own acceptable-use policies and incident response procedures with the legal standards OpenAI is now documenting publicly.

2026-05-31.summary: GitHub Copilot switches all plans to AI Credits token billing in under 24 hours as Claude Code 2.1.158 extends Auto mode to Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry and DeepSeek permanently locks its 75 percent V4 Pro price cut.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot token billing replaces flat premium requests across all plans in under 24 hours
items.description: On June 1, all GitHub Copilot plans move from premium request units (PRUs) to AI Credits, where every model interaction is billed at the underlying model's API rate (1 credit = $0.01). Pro ($29/mo), Pro+ ($39/mo), Business ($19/user/mo) and Enterprise ($39/user/mo) each receive a monthly AI Credits allotment equal to their plan cost in dollars; interactions beyond the allotment consume pay-as-you-go credits. Free and Student plan users on monthly billing are automatically migrated today; annual subscribers stay on PRU pricing until their term ends. Heavier usage of Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5, or Gemini 3.5 Flash inside Copilot will exceed allotments faster than GPT-4.1 mini, which is included at no credit cost.
items.action: Log into Billing Overview on github.com now to see the projected AI Credits preview for your team; set a spending limit before midnight to avoid unbounded credit charges on June 1.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.158 extends Auto mode to Bedrock, Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry for Opus 4.7 and 4.8
items.description: Auto mode, which dynamically selects effort level and subagent count for each task, is now available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry for Claude Opus 4.7 and Opus 4.8. Teams on cloud-hosted Claude must opt in via the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 environment variable; the default remains manual mode on these platforms. This closes the gap with direct Claude API deployments, where Auto mode shipped alongside Opus 4.8 on May 29. The release also carries 50+ bug fixes across worktree management, background sessions, and cross-platform issues.
items.action: Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 in your Bedrock or Vertex Claude Code environment to enable adaptive task planning; test with Opus 4.8 first as it defaults effort to high.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex Pro 2x usage promotion expires today reverting capacity to standard 5x for Plus
items.description: The promotional doubling of Codex capacity that launched with ChatGPT Pro in April ends on May 31. After today, the $100/month Pro plan reverts from 10x Plus usage to the standard 5x, and the 5-hour Codex window at 25x Plus drops to 20x. The $200/month Pro tier retains its 2x multiplier as a permanent benefit. Teams that built Codex-heavy workflows under the doubled limits will see execution quotas halved starting June 1, which may surface as rate limit errors on long-running agentic tasks.
items.action: Audit Codex task queue depths and rate limit headroom before June 1; consider moving high-volume Codex tasks to the Codex CLI via API key if Pro plan limits are no longer sufficient.

items.headline: DeepSeek V4 Pro permanent pricing confirmed at 75 percent below launch price as promotional window closes
items.description: DeepSeek's API documentation confirms the promotional discount introduced at the V4 Pro launch is permanent, with V4 Pro now priced at $0.435 per million input tokens and $0.87 per million output tokens as of May 31. The discount will not revert now that the original promotional expiry date has passed. At $0.87 per million output tokens, V4 Pro is 34.5x cheaper than GPT-5.5 ($30/1M output) and 10x cheaper than Claude Opus 4.8 ($25/1M output) while delivering comparable coding and reasoning results on SWE-Bench Pro.
items.action: Benchmark DeepSeek V4 Pro on your highest-volume reasoning and coding agent tasks; the permanent pricing makes it viable as a primary model for cost-sensitive production pipelines that can tolerate Chinese data routing.

2026-06-01.summary: GitHub Copilot AI Credits billing goes live ending flat PRU pricing as OpenAI extends Codex computer use to Windows and announces the last GPT-4.x models will leave ChatGPT by August.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot AI Credits billing goes live replacing flat premium requests across all plans
items.description: All GitHub Copilot plans switched to token-based AI Credits billing effective today. Monthly allotments match subscription price: Pro gets $10, Pro+ $39, Business $19 per user, Enterprise $39 per user. items.action: Review your billing overview at github.com to see projected costs under the new model. Set a monthly spend cap if you run high-volume agent workloads, since heavy use of Claude Opus or GPT-5 class models will consume allotments faster than the flat PRU model did. Unused credits do not roll over.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex brings computer use to Windows with mobile remote steering and usage profiles
items.description: Codex app version 26.527 ships foreground computer use on Windows, letting the agent see the screen and drive keyboard and mouse across native Windows desktop apps. Remote continuation from iOS, Android, or Mac now lets users start or steer Windows Codex sessions from a phone. New Codex Profiles surface per-thread token activity and usage history for cost tracking.
items.action: Windows users can now run Codex agentic tasks on native apps without a Mac or VM workaround. Note the foreground-only constraint: Codex cannot quietly background-operate Windows sessions while you use the same machine. Computer use is not available in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland at launch.

items.headline: OpenAI schedules GPT-4.5 and o3 retirement from ChatGPT as last GPT-4 era models depart
items.description: GPT-4.5 will be removed from ChatGPT on June 27 following a 30-day sunset and o3 will follow on August 26 after a 90-day window. Both remain accessible only to paid users via ChatGPT model settings until their respective dates. No API changes are planned; the retirements affect the ChatGPT UI only and clear the interface for GPT-5 class models.
items.action: Brief users or internal teams relying on GPT-4.5 or o3 through the ChatGPT UI on the June 27 and August 26 deadlines. No migration is needed for API workloads as these retirements are ChatGPT-only.

2026-06-02.summary: Microsoft Build 2026 keynote cuts GitHub Copilot loose from OpenAI with Project Polaris in August and open-sources the Windows Agent Framework; Codex CLI and Copilot CLI ship stable updates.

items.headline: Microsoft replaces OpenAI in GitHub Copilot with Project Polaris from August 2026
items.description: At Build 2026, Microsoft unveiled Project Polaris, a proprietary mixture-of-experts model with language-specific sub-modules, as the new default reasoning engine for GitHub Copilot, replacing GPT-4 Turbo from August 2026. Automatic migration happens with no action required; teams get a three-month opt-out window to stay on GPT-4 while the transition completes. This ends Microsoft's dependence on OpenAI inference for its flagship developer tool and marks the first time Copilot runs on a non-OpenAI model by default.
items.action: Audit Copilot quality benchmarks and prompting guides tuned to GPT-4 Turbo behavior before August; plan a validation sprint on Polaris outputs when the beta becomes available for testing.

items.headline: Windows Agent Framework goes MIT, Copilot Workspace exits beta, Windows Agent Store opens at Build 2026
items.description: Microsoft open-sourced the Windows Agent Framework under an MIT license, making the agent lifecycle library available for building agents that run across local Windows machines, Windows 365 Cloud PCs, and Azure Arc-enabled edge devices. Copilot Workspace moved to general availability, letting developers file a plain-language issue and receive a multi-file plan, diff, and pull request without writing a line of code. The Windows Agent Store launched as a curated marketplace for agent manifests with security reviews enforced and an 85 percent revenue share for developers.
items.action: Evaluate Windows Agent Framework for enterprise clients on Windows 365 or Azure Arc. Explore Copilot Workspace GA for offloading repetitive issue-to-PR pipelines. List agent manifests on the Windows Agent Store if building for Windows-first enterprise workflows.

items.headline: WSL 3 re-architecture gives AI workloads near-native GPU and NPU access on Windows
items.description: Microsoft announced WSL 3 at Build 2026, a complete re-architecture that moves the Linux kernel into a lightweight VM with paravirtualized access to the Windows GPU and NPU. AI and ML workloads running inside WSL now operate at near-native speed without GPU passthrough workarounds. Azure Agent Mesh was also announced as a control plane for federated agent execution across Windows servers, Cloud PCs, and Azure Arc, targeting Q4 2026 general availability.
items.action: Plan WSL 3 adoption for any ML team running local training or inference in WSL on Windows machines. Monitor Azure Agent Mesh preview for builders managing hybrid on-premises and cloud agent deployments.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.136.0 adds session archiving and closes supply chain attack vector in diff tool
items.description: Codex CLI 0.136.0 shipped June 1 with session archiving via an /archive command, TUI markdown rendering with clickable web links, and a security fix preventing /diff from executing repository-provided Git helpers, closing a vector where malicious repo-side scripts could run during diff operations. ChatGPT auth now proactively refreshes tokens before the expiry window, eliminating mid-session auth failures in long-running agentic tasks.
items.action: Update Codex CLI to 0.136.0 immediately for the /diff security fix. Session archiving enables cost-effective storage of long coding sessions for audit or replay.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.57 terminates process trees on shell command cancellation
items.description: Version 1.0.57 released June 1 fixes orphaned process handling by terminating the full process tree when a shell command is cancelled, preventing background resource leaks in long-running agent sessions. Canvas providers now accept file:// URLs enabling local file preview without an HTTP server, and HTTP/1.1 is set as the default networking transport for more reliable operation behind proxies.
items.action: Update to 1.0.57 if running Copilot CLI in automated pipelines or CI environments where cancelled commands previously left orphaned processes.

2026-06-03.summary: OpenAI brings GPT-5.5 and Codex to Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft debuts its first reasoning model MAI-Thinking-1 at Build 2026, and MiniMax ships an open-weight model combining frontier coding with 1M context and multimodality.

items.headline: OpenAI GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 and Codex go generally available on Amazon Bedrock
items.description: GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 are now GA on Amazon Bedrock alongside Codex, giving AWS customers access to OpenAI frontier models through existing IAM, VPC, procurement, and compliance workflows. GPT-5.5 is live in US East (Ohio) and GPT-5.4 in two regions; Codex routes inference through Bedrock across its app, CLI, and IDE surfaces. Enterprises no longer need separate OpenAI accounts or direct API contracts to run frontier models in production.

items.headline: Microsoft debuts MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model and six companion MAI models at Build 2026
items.description: Microsoft's AI Superintelligence Team released seven in-house models at Build 2026, anchored by MAI-Thinking-1: a 35B active parameter reasoning model with 256K context, trained without distillation on commercially licensed data and matching Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro. Companion releases include MAI-Code-1 for GitHub, MAI-Image-2.5 for text-to-image and image-to-image workflows, MAI-Voice-2 in 15 additional languages, and MAI-Transcribe-1.5 across 43 languages. items.headline: MiniMax M3 launches as first open-weight model combining frontier coding, 1M context and multimodality
items.description: MiniMax released M3 on June 1 via API, claiming the first open-weight model to unify frontier-level coding, a 1-million-token context window, and native multimodality in a single release using a sparse MSA architecture. M3 tops the open-weight SWE-Bench Pro leaderboard at 59.0%. Open weights and a technical report are due on Hugging Face within ten days of launch.
items.action: Test M3 via the MiniMax API now; plan self-hosted integration once weights land on Hugging Face around June 10-11 for long-context multimodal and agentic coding workflows.

items.headline: Claude API adds advisor tool output cap and stops billing on refusal responses
items.description: Two platform changes landed on June 2: the advisor tool now accepts a max_tokens parameter to hard-cap advisor model output per call, reducing latency and output token cost in Opus-advises-Sonnet orchestration patterns. Separately, API requests that return stop_reason of refusal without generating any output are no longer charged.
items.action: Add max_tokens to advisor tool definitions in production to tune cost against quality; remove any billing workarounds built around refusal responses in cost tracking code.

items.headline: Claude Code renames workflow trigger to ultracode and adds shell startup write prompts in v2.1.160 and v2.1.161

The release also prompts before writing to shell startup files (.zshenv, .bash_login) and build-tool config files (.npmrc, .yarnrc). v2.1.161 adds OTEL resource attributes as metric labels for custom dimension slicing and prevents a failed parallel Bash call from cancelling sibling calls in the same batch.

items.headline: OpenAI workspace agents gain GPT-5.5, role-based publishing and enterprise app templates
items.description: ChatGPT Business and Enterprise workspace agents now support GPT-5.5 with configurable reasoning effort controls, audio file output, and role-based publishing for the shared agent directory. App templates with guided setup are available for GitHub Enterprise, Snowflake, and Databricks. The free usage period for workspace agents has been extended to July 6.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI ships scheduled prompt commands and on-device voice dictation in v1.0.58 and v1.0.59
items.description: v1.0.58 (June 2) enables the Rubber Duck agent and remote JSON-RPC by default and adds experimental /every and /after commands for scheduling recurring or delayed prompts inside CLI sessions. v1.0.59 adds a /voice command that transcribes speech using a local model, keeping audio data on device without a cloud STT API.

items.headline: Gemini 3.5 Flash becomes mandatory in Gemini Enterprise on June 8 as admin toggle is removed
items.description: Starting June 8, the feature management toggle allowing admins to disable Gemini 3.5 Flash in the Gemini Enterprise app will be removed; the model becomes enabled by default and cannot be turned off. Gemini 3.5 Flash launched at Google I/O on May 19 at $1.50/$9 per million input/output tokens, triple the prior Gemini 3 Flash pricing.
items.action: Review Gemini Enterprise workspace configurations before June 8; update budget models to reflect the 3x pricing uplift if Gemini 3.5 Flash was not previously enabled.

2026-06-04.summary: OpenAI turns Codex into a hosted app platform with role plugins at Intelligence at Work, Anthropic expands Project Glasswing cybersecurity AI to 150 organizations across 15 countries, and Microsoft ships a kernel-level agent sandbox for Windows at Build 2026.

items.headline: OpenAI adds hosted app builder, six role plugins and Annotations to Codex as it enters ChatGPT app
items.description: At the Intelligence at Work event on June 2, OpenAI shipped three Codex capability layers: Sites (Business and Enterprise preview) lets Codex deploy interactive dashboards, internal tools, and web apps hosted by OpenAI directly from prompts; six role-specific plugins for finance, legal, HR, sales, operations, and research teams; and Annotations for in-document collaboration across documents, spreadsheets, and slides. Codex is also being embedded inside the ChatGPT app, putting all these capabilities at an existing five million weekly user base.
items.action: Evaluate Sites as a deployment endpoint for Codex-generated dashboards and data apps; review role plugins for overlap with existing Make.com or n8n workflows serving knowledge workers. The ChatGPT embed means non-technical stakeholders can now trigger Codex runs without a separate account.

items.headline: Anthropic expands Project Glasswing to 150 organizations across 15 countries as Mythos finds 10,000 critical vulnerabilities
items.description: Anthropic is extending Claude Mythos access to approximately 150 new organizations in more than 15 countries, adding sectors underrepresented at launch: power, water, healthcare, communications, and hardware. Named new participants include NATO, the EU cybersecurity agency ENISA, Okta, Samsung, SK Hynix, and SK Telecom. Since the program began, Glasswing partners have surfaced more than 10,000 high or critical-severity vulnerabilities in production systems.
items.action: Builders in regulated or critical infrastructure sectors should submit Glasswing applications now that the program is open beyond the initial launch cohort. Monitor partner disclosures for vulnerability patterns affecting shared open-source dependencies in your stacks.

items.headline: Microsoft ships MXC kernel sandbox for AI agents with process, session and micro-VM isolation on Windows
items.description: Announced at Build 2026, Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) is a policy-driven execution layer baked into the Windows kernel that lets developers define exactly what an AI agent can access at runtime. It supports three isolation levels: fast process isolation (already adopted by GitHub Copilot CLI), session isolation that binds the agent to a strong user identity to block UI spoofing and input injection, and micro-VM isolation backed by the hypervisor for high-risk workloads. OpenAI Codex and Nvidia are already on board; Defender, Entra, Intune, and Purview integration arrives in July preview.
items.action: Architects building Windows-hosted AI agents should read the MXC policy model before the July Intune preview. The containment granularity directly addresses TrustFall- and SymJack-class attacks at the OS level, making it relevant for enterprise agent deployments where SymJack mitigations in individual tools are not enough.

items.headline: Trump signs voluntary AI model pre-release review order and establishes AI cybersecurity clearinghouse
items.description: Signed June 2, the executive order asks AI companies on a voluntary basis to submit frontier models for a government cybersecurity capability assessment up to 30 days before public release; models deemed covered frontier models face additional scrutiny. A new AI Cybersecurity Clearinghouse will coordinate with industry and critical infrastructure operators to identify and remediate software vulnerabilities at scale. The order expressly prohibits any mandatory licensing, pre-clearance, or permitting requirement for AI development or distribution.
items.action: Builders at enterprises selling AI products or services to US government agencies should monitor the voluntary review process; the clearinghouse creates a new official channel for vulnerability disclosures that could accelerate patch availability for infrastructure libraries.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.162 surfaces agent wait state, dedicated search tools and Remote Control status pill
items.description: Released June 3, v2.1.162 adds a waitingFor field to claude agents --json output so orchestration scripts can distinguish blocked agents from working ones. Explicitly listing Grep or Glob in --tools now provisions dedicated search tools on native builds with embedded search, and the /effort command confirms when a chosen level persists as the session default. Slash command autocomplete now fills the prompt without auto-executing, requiring an Enter keystroke.
items.action: Update any monitoring pipeline using claude agents --json to inspect the new waitingFor field for early detection of stalled permission prompts. Review --tools declarations in any Claude Code wrapper that expects search capabilities on native builds.

2026-06-05.summary: GitHub Copilot opens its agent runtime as a general-purpose SDK across six languages and adds a one-million-token context window with configurable reasoning, transforming it from an IDE plugin into a developer platform.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot SDK reaches general availability in six languages with MCP and BYOK support
items.description: GitHub shipped the Copilot SDK to general availability on June 2, giving developers programmatic access to the same agent runtime that powers GitHub Copilot, including planning, tool invocation, file edits, streaming, and multi-turn sessions. Available in Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java, the SDK supports custom tool registration, MCP server connections, and multi-client sessions where different clients contribute tools to the same agent session. Non-Copilot users can access it via BYOK, and all existing Copilot subscribers including the free plan gain access at no extra charge.
items.action: Replace custom orchestration layers with the Copilot SDK if you are building editor-integrated or CLI-integrated agents; the MCP connector support means existing MCP tool surfaces plug directly into Copilot's planning loop without rewiring.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot gains one-million-token context and configurable reasoning across VS Code, CLI and Copilot app
items.description: GitHub expanded Copilot on June 4 with a one-million-token context window available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app, enabling full-codebase analysis without truncation on the largest codebases. Configurable reasoning levels let developers dial between speed and extended thinking depth for architectural and debugging problems, consuming more AI credits per interaction at higher settings. A separate June 4 changelog entry also extends Fix with Copilot for failing Actions to Pro, Pro+, and Max plans, letting Copilot diagnose and suggest fixes for failing GitHub Actions runs.
items.action: Use the 1M context window for whole-repo refactoring, migration audits, and large schema analysis that previously required chunking; enable extended reasoning for architecture reviews while keeping low reasoning for routine edits to manage credit spend.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.163 adds managed version lock settings and MCP session identity for enterprise deployments
items.description: Released June 4 at 21:52 UTC, v2.1.163 adds requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion fields to managed settings, letting administrators pin Claude Code to a specific version range across an organization. Hooks can now return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext to feed feedback back into the agent without flagging it as an error, and stdio MCP servers receive CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID on --resume so server-side session continuity is preserved across reconnects. The release also fixes claude -p hanging after the final result, Bash failures under Bazel and EDR-protected workflows, and Windows file permission errors on session-env directories.
items.action: If you manage Claude Code across a team, set requiredMinimumVersion now to prevent version drift; if you build Claude Code hooks or MCP servers, update to pass additionalContext and read the session ID for continuity tracking.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.137.0 ships multi-agent v2 runtime and enterprise monthly credit limit controls
items.description: The stable v0.137.0 release on June 4 upgrades the multi-agent runtime to v2, which keeps model selection with each spawned thread and cleans up follow-up and metadata defaults across agent hierarchies. Remote-control client pairing is now available via app-server v2 RPCs, enabling controllers to list and revoke pairing grants programmatically. Enterprise and admin flows gain visibility into monthly credit limits and can apply cloud-managed config bundles including EDU workspace settings; TUI markdown now renders clickable links and supports F13 through F24 keybindings.
items.action: Upgrade to v0.137.0 if you run multi-agent Codex pipelines; the v2 runtime changes thread-level model selection so test existing orchestration scripts against changed defaults before rolling to production.

items.headline: GPT-Rosalind expands to global API access with 31 percent lower token cost for genomics workloads
items.description: OpenAI published substantial updates to GPT-Rosalind on June 3, opening the life-sciences model to eligible organizations worldwide and adding Codex plugins connecting researchers to over 50 scientific databases spanning genomics, transcriptomics, and structural biology. Three new evaluations show the updated model completes quantitative biology analyses using 31 percent fewer tokens than GPT-5.5, lowering cost for high-volume research pipelines. Novo Nordisk joined earlier partners Amgen, Moderna, Allen Institute, and Thermo Fisher Scientific in the program.
items.action: If you build automation workflows for pharma, biotech, or clinical research clients, evaluate GPT-Rosalind as a drop-in for general-purpose model calls on biology-heavy tasks to reduce token spend.

items.headline: OpenAI retires Agent Builder, Evals platform and reusable prompt objects by November 30
items.description: OpenAI notified developers on June 3 of three simultaneous deprecations: Agent Builder and the Evals platform become read-only October 31 and shut down November 30, 2026; the v1/prompts reusable prompt objects API also shuts down November 30. Agent Builder users must migrate to the Agents SDK or ChatGPT Workspace Agents; Evals users must build custom evaluation pipelines; prompt objects must move into application code where versioning is fully developer-controlled.
items.action: Audit any production workflows using OpenAI Agent Builder, the Evals API, or v1/prompts. Begin migration to Agents SDK for agentic workloads and remove prompt object dependencies before October 31 read-only cutover.

items.headline: Claude Opus 4.1 deprecated with 60-day countdown to August 5 retirement
items.description: Anthropic announced on June 5 via the primary deprecation page that claude-opus-4-1-20250805 is deprecated effective today, with a retirement date of August 5, 2026. The recommended replacement is claude-opus-4-8, which is already the default on Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and the API. Any workflow hardcoded to the 4.1 model string will begin failing in 60 days.
items.action: Search codebases and API configurations for claude-opus-4-1-20250805 and replace with claude-opus-4-8. The deprecation page now also shows that temperature, top_p, and top_k are API errors on Opus 4.7 and later.

items.headline: OpenAI macOS app signing certificates expire June 12 forcing update deadline
items.description: Following the May 11 TanStack npm supply chain attack in which TeamPCP exfiltrated credentials from two OpenAI employee devices, OpenAI is revoking compromised code-signing certificates on June 12. After that date, macOS Gatekeeper will block launches of any ChatGPT Desktop, Codex App, Codex CLI, or Atlas build signed with the old certificate. Windows and iOS users are unaffected.
items.action: Update all macOS OpenAI desktop apps before June 12. Builders running Codex CLI in macOS CI pipelines must update the binary or add the new certificate to trust stores before the revocation date or automated pipelines will break.

items.headline: OpenAI replaces ChatGPT saved memories with Dreaming V3 background synthesis architecture
items.description: OpenAI began rolling out Dreaming V3 on June 4 for ChatGPT Plus and Pro users in the US, replacing the manually curated saved-memories list with a background synthesis process that reads across conversation history and updates itself automatically over time. A hierarchical memory structure separates short-term conversation context from long-term user knowledge, allowing memories to stay current without user prompting. OpenAI published the Memory API and invited external privacy researchers to review its guarantees.
items.action: Builders integrating ChatGPT into workflows that depend on explicit user-managed memory should review the new Memory API documentation. Expect ChatGPT to behave differently for long-term users as background synthesis accumulates context that was previously only in saved notes.

2026-06-07.summary: Miasma worm plants credential harvesting payloads in 73 Microsoft Azure GitHub repositories targeting Claude Code and Gemini CLI users; OpenAI launches Lockdown Mode for ChatGPT; Claude Code gains fallback model resilience; Gemini Interactions API legacy schema permanently removed June 8.

items.headline: Miasma worm plants credential harvesting payloads in 73 Microsoft Azure GitHub repositories targeting AI coding tools
items.description: On June 5, the Miasma self-replicating supply chain worm reached Microsoft's Azure GitHub organizations, planting config files in 73 repositories across Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, and MicrosoftDocs that silently harvest developer credentials when a repository is opened in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code. GitHub's automated systems disabled all 73 affected repos in 105 seconds, but any developer who cloned between June 4 and June 5 and opened the repo in an affected tool may have had credentials exfiltrated. Miasma is assessed as a variant of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm family tied to the same campaign as the May TanStack supply chain attack.
items.action: Audit any repositories cloned from the Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, or MicrosoftDocs GitHub organizations between June 4 and June 5 for unexpected changes to CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, or .vscode/settings.json. Rotate API keys, GitHub tokens, and cloud credentials for any machine where affected repos were opened in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code during that window.

items.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Lockdown Mode to block prompt injection data exfiltration for all accounts
items.description: OpenAI launched Lockdown Mode on June 6, an opt-in security setting available to all ChatGPT accounts that disables web browsing, agent mode, deep research, file downloads, external connectors, and canvas networking to block the final exfiltration stage of prompt injection attacks. Enterprise admins can enforce Lockdown Mode workspace-wide via RBAC and the Compliance API. Lockdown Mode and Developer Mode are mutually exclusive: enabling one disables the other, so any enterprise workflow using Developer Mode must choose between agentic capability and network lockdown.
items.action: Review enterprise ChatGPT agentic workflows that rely on web access, agent mode, or file downloads before rolling out Lockdown Mode to users. Document the security tradeoff for clients: Lockdown Mode stops exfiltration but breaks multi-step agent tasks that require external data fetching.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.166 adds fallback model configuration with three model cascade and global tool deny glob
items.description: Claude Code v2.1.166 (June 6, 00:55 UTC) adds a fallbackModel setting that lets builders configure up to three fallback models that are activated automatically when the primary model is overloaded or unavailable, enabling resilient production deployments without custom retry logic. Glob pattern support in deny rules now allows using a wildcard to deny all tools in a single rule, which simplifies locked-down execution environments. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 and the new --thinking disabled flag now correctly disable thinking on default-thinking models such as Opus 4.8.
items.action: Add a fallbackModel array to your Claude Code project config pointing to claude-sonnet-4-6 or claude-opus-4-7 as failover targets for Opus 4.8 deployments. Use the wildcard deny glob in high-security automation contexts where no shell access should be granted.

items.headline: Gemini Interactions API permanently removes legacy outputs schema June 8 with no opt-out remaining
items.description: The legacy outputs response format in the Gemini Interactions API is permanently removed June 8, 2026, one day from today. All applications using the legacy schema that have not migrated to the steps format or upgraded to Python SDK 2.0.0 or JavaScript SDK 2.0.0 will receive errors after the cutoff. items.action: Immediately audit all Gemini Interactions API integrations. Upgrading Python SDK to 2.0.0 or JavaScript SDK to 2.0.0 automatically handles the new steps schema with no code changes to response reading. If you cannot upgrade today, add the Api-Revision: 2026-05-07 header as an emergency stopgap before the June 8 cutoff, then migrate fully this week.

2026-06-08.summary: Apple opens iOS 27 AI layer to Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT as system-level providers at WWDC 2026; Google Interactions API legacy schema permanently removed; Anthropic Agent SDK credit claim email arrives with one week to act before June 15 billing split.

items.headline: Apple opens iOS 27 AI layer to Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT as system providers
items.description: At WWDC 2026, Apple announced iOS 27 Extensions, a system-wide framework letting users set Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT as the AI provider for Siri, Writing Tools, and Image Playground across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27. This is the first time Apple has made third-party AI a first-class OS citizen; Claude-based products can now reach users without requiring a separate app launch.

items.description: Today is the hard removal date for the legacy outputs array in the Gemini Interactions API. There is no opt-out header available after today. items.action: Audit Gemini Interactions API integrations for any remaining outputs usage. If calls are failing today, migrate to the steps schema or upgrade to SDK 2.0.0 and above which handles the migration automatically.

items.description: Effective today, the feature management toggle that allowed workspace admins to disable Gemini 3.5 Flash for users is no longer available in the Gemini Enterprise app. Gemini 3.5 Flash is now permanently enabled by default and cannot be turned off across all regions including Global, US, and EU multi-regions.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.169 ships safe-mode isolation and cache-preserving directory switch
items.description: The --safe-mode flag and CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE environment variable disable all customizations including CLAUDE.md, plugins, skills, hooks, and MCP servers for clean troubleshooting without touching project files. The new /cd command moves a session to a new working directory while keeping the prompt cache intact, eliminating the cold-start cost when switching between project roots mid-session. Enterprise MCP policy enforcement via allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers is now correctly applied on reconnect and IDE-typed configs, closing a security gap for managed deployments.
items.action: Add --safe-mode to CI steps that run Claude Code in sandboxed or restricted environments. Use /cd instead of opening a new session when navigating between repos to keep cache warm. Verify enterprise MCP policies are enforced correctly after reconnect in multi-repo setups.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.138.0 ships desktop handoff and image path exposure for agent pipelines
items.description: The /app command routes a Codex CLI session to a native macOS or Windows desktop application, enabling agents to interact with GUI tools and system-level APIs unavailable from the terminal. items.action: Test /app handoff if your pipelines involve GUI-dependent tools on macOS or Windows. Review token usage reporting in app-server mode if you run Codex in CI pipelines with cost budgets.

2026-06-10.summary: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5, first publicly available Mythos-class model at $10/$50 per million tokens with new stop_reason refusal handling and opt-in model fallbacks; CLI tooling updates across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Copilot CLI ship Fable 5 routing on the same day.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5, first publicly available Mythos-class model
items.description: Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) is live on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, double Opus 4.8 pricing. The model uses the same tokenizer as Opus 4.7, generating roughly 30 percent more tokens than pre-4.7 models on identical text, meaning existing prompts cost more without adjustment. New API behavior: when safety classifiers decline a request in cybersecurity, biology, chemistry, or distillation domains, the Messages API returns HTTP 200 with stop_reason: refusal; an opt-in fallbacks parameter in beta re-runs refused requests on a fallback model at that model's rate. items.action: Audit all existing prompts using the token counting API with model: claude-fable-5 before switching to size cost impact from the new tokenizer. Add stop_reason refusal handling to error-handling and retry logic in any pipeline that calls Fable 5. Review the fallbacks parameter for automated workflows that may touch cybersecurity or bio/chem domains. Enable usage credits before June 23 if you want subscription plan access to Fable 5 after the free window closes.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.139.0 ships standalone web search in code mode and fixes MCP tool schema flattening

items.headline: Claude Managed Agents ships native cron scheduling and vault-secured credential injection

Scheduled deployments run under existing Claude Platform usage pricing with no separate charge. The two features together address the two most common reasons enterprise agent pilots stall: automated triggering and secure service authentication.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.172 lets sub-agents spawn their own sub-agents up to five levels deep
items.description: Before v2.1.172, sub-agents in Claude Code were terminal: they could not delegate further, capping agent hierarchies at two levels. The new release lifts that constraint, allowing up to five levels of nested spawning so a coordinator agent can hand work to specialists that in turn spawn their own workers. items.action: Update to 2.1.172 to access nested sub-agent spawning for complex multi-agent orchestration. If you use Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock and set your region via ~/.aws config rather than an environment variable, verify Bedrock connectivity after updating.

OAuth flows now support RFC 8707 resource parameter, improving compatibility with stricter enterprise authorisation servers. Workflow activation stability is improved to prevent unexpected trigger firing during startup, and security dependencies including nodemailer are updated to 8.0.10.
items.action: Schedule a maintenance window before upgrading to 2.27.0 on instances with large execution history. The DB migration is automatic but blocking. Test any OAuth credential flows against RFC 8707 strict servers that were previously failing.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.63 adds experimental rewind without git and fork PR visibility
items.description: Version 1.0.63 introduces an experimental rewind feature that restores only session-modified files without requiring a git repository, making it usable in non-git or gitignored project layouts. Fork-based PR visibility now surfaces pull requests from forked repositories in diff and PR commands. Whitespace is hidden in diffs by default and auth error messages surface the specific failure reason rather than a generic prompt.
items.action: Test rewind on non-git project directories as an alternative to manual state rollback. The feature is experimental and behavior may change in future releases. Fork PR visibility is relevant if you regularly review upstream changes in forked monorepos.

2026-06-18.summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash reaches general availability in the Gemini API alongside Managed Agents public preview; US export controls on Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 enter day six with no announced resolution.

items.headline: Gemini 3.5 Flash goes GA in Gemini API alongside Managed Agents and Antigravity Agent public preview
items.description: Google updated the Gemini API on June 17 to mark gemini-3.5-flash as generally available, lifting preview-tier limitations and locking in SLA guarantees for production workloads. The same release launched Managed Agents in public preview, giving API developers Google-hosted isolated Linux sandboxes for stateful autonomous agents, a direct parallel to Anthropic Managed Agents. The general-purpose Antigravity Agent (antigravity-preview-05-2026) is also in public preview and can plan, write and execute code, manage files, and browse the web inside its container.
items.action: Update production pipelines from gemini-3.5-flash-preview to gemini-3.5-flash for SLA coverage. Evaluate Managed Agents API for use cases currently handled by self-hosted sandboxes. Note: gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview and gemini-3-pro-image-preview are deprecated and shut down June 25.

items.headline: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 remain suspended under US export controls as Anthropic-government talks continue
items.description: The US Commerce Department Bureau of Industry and Security invoked the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 on June 12, requiring Anthropic to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national inside or outside the US, citing a claimed jailbreak of Fable 5 cybersecurity guardrails. Unable to verify nationality in real time, Anthropic disabled both models globally, making this the first US government-mandated withdrawal of a commercially available AI model. Anthropic met with Commerce Department officials June 14-16 to negotiate terms; as of June 18 both models remain offline with no announced restoration date.
items.action: Do not plan new workloads on Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) or Mythos 5 until further notice. Use Claude Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 4.6 as replacements. Monitor Anthropic status page for restoration updates.

items.headline: Gemini CLI stops serving requests as Antigravity CLI becomes the only Google AI terminal client
items.description: As of June 18, Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions have stopped serving requests for all Google AI Pro, Google AI Ultra, and free Gemini Code Assist for individuals users. The Antigravity CLI (agy) is the required replacement, offering Go-based startup speed, parallel subagent orchestration, /goal and /schedule slash commands, and Gemini 3.5 Flash as the default model. Enterprise users on Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licenses and paid API key holders are unaffected.
items.action: Run agy --version to confirm Antigravity CLI is installed. If gemini commands return errors, install Antigravity CLI immediately. Rename GEMINI.md to AGENTS.md and .gemini/skills/ to .agents/skills/ to migrate project configuration.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.181 adds /config prompt syntax and upgrades bundled Bun to 1.4
items.description: Released June 17 at 22:07 UTC, v2.1.181 lets users set any Claude Code setting directly from the prompt with /config key=value syntax, removing the need to open settings files for ad-hoc overrides. The bundled Bun runtime is upgraded to 1.4 and streaming of long paragraphs is improved with line-by-line display. Additional changes include sandbox.allowAppleEvents for macOS automation and CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE to suppress mobile push notifications in shared or remote environments.
items.action: Run claude update to get 2.1.181. Use /config key=value for quick session-level setting overrides without editing settings.json.

2026-06-19.summary: Anthropic reversed its Agent SDK billing split before it took effect, leaving subscription usage unchanged; Fable 5 export suspension enters day seven with Washington talks active and a June 20 refund deadline; Codex CLI 0.141.0 ships encrypted remote execution channels.

items.headline: Anthropic reverses Agent SDK billing split on the day it was due to take effect
items.description: Anthropic paused its planned June 15 billing overhaul for the Agent SDK, the claude -p command, and third-party Claude apps on the same day it was scheduled to go live, emailing developers that nothing changes for now and that the company is working to better align pricing with actual usage patterns. The planned change would have created separate monthly credit pools (0 Pro, 00 Max 5x, 00 Max 20x) that would have been exhausted before overflow billing began. Agent SDK usage, claude -p, and third-party apps continue drawing from regular subscription limits as before, indefinitely until Anthropic reschedules.
items.action: No billing changes are required. If you modified agent pipelines or disabled Agent SDK usage in response to the June 15 announcement, you can safely revert those changes. Watch for a new announcement date before making further billing adjustments.

items.headline: Fable 5 suspension enters day seven as Washington talks advance and refund window closes June 20
items.description: Anthropic dispatched senior technical staff to Washington for in-person talks with Commerce Department officials; as of June 17 negotiations were described as progressing with informal reports suggesting restoration could come within 24 to 48 hours, though neither Anthropic nor Commerce has issued an official timeline. Subscribers who signed up for a Claude plan June 9 to 14 expecting Fable 5 access have until June 20 to request refunds for the unavailable period. Anthropic has not issued updated pricing guidance for when Fable 5 returns.
items.action: If you subscribed to any Claude plan June 9 to 14, request a refund from Anthropic before June 20. Continue using claude-opus-4-8 as the highest available model tier. Do not build new production workflows on Fable 5 until Anthropic confirms restoration.

items.headline: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.141.0 adds encrypted Noise relay channels for remote execution
items.description: Codex CLI 0.141.0 (released June 18, 04:43 UTC) routes remote executor traffic through authenticated, end-to-end encrypted Noise relay channels, removing the need for VPN or direct network access when connecting remote sandboxes. Cross-platform remote execution now preserves the executor-native working directory and shell environment so macOS, Linux, and Windows executors behave consistently regardless of where the CLI runs. Plugin discovery gains marketplace features with auth-specific catalogs, making it easier to scope installed plugins to specific identity contexts.
items.action: Update Codex CLI to 0.141.0 via npm for remote execution security improvements. Enterprise teams running Codex against private compute environments can now connect without VPN, reducing network provisioning overhead.

2026-06-20.summary: Anthropic brings enterprise MCP authorization to stable with zero-touch Okta provisioning; Claude Code 2.1.183 gates destructive git and IaC commands in auto mode; Claude Design adds bidirectional Claude Code sync; Veo 3.0 enters 10-day shutdown window.

items.headline: Anthropic makes enterprise MCP auth stable removing per-user OAuth across seven SaaS providers
items.description: Anthropic launched Enterprise-Managed Authorization for Claude MCP connectors on June 18, giving IT admins a single provisioning step through Okta that pushes connector access to all employees on first login with no individual OAuth prompts. Seven providers support the standard at launch: Asana, Atlassian, Canva, Figma, Granola, Linear, and Supabase. The underlying spec was adopted by the IETF OAuth working group in September 2025, incorporated into the MCP specification in November 2025, and is now declared stable as a formal MCP authorization extension.
items.action: Enterprise teams on Claude Team or Enterprise plan can enable EMA in the admin console now. New hires automatically inherit all approved MCP connectors without IT tickets. Check which of the seven supported providers your stack uses and provision once.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.183 blocks git reset hard and infrastructure destroy commands in auto mode
items.description: Claude Code v2.1.183 (June 19) adds an auto-mode safety classifier that blocks git reset --hard, git checkout -- ., git clean -fd, and git stash drop unless explicitly requested, plus git commit --amend when the prior commit was not made in the current session. Terraform, Pulumi, and CDK destroy commands are similarly gated. The release also adds model deprecation warnings to stderr in print mode and an attribution.sessionUrl setting to strip claude.ai session links from automated commits.
items.action: Upgrade to 2.1.183. Audit any auto-mode pipelines that relied on unchallenged destructive git operations. Use attribution.sessionUrl: false in settings if session URLs in commit messages are unwanted.

items.headline: Claude Design major overhaul adds design system imports and bidirectional sync with Claude Code
items.description: Anthropic shipped a major Claude Design update on June 17 adding importable design systems from GitHub repos or file uploads, a /design-sync command that creates a bidirectional round-trip between the Claude Code terminal and the Claude Design canvas, and direct WYSIWYG canvas editing. The update also addresses the token-burning problem where repeated regeneration cycles consumed excessive context unnecessarily. Rolling out in beta to paid Claude users.
items.action: Teams using Claude Design alongside Claude Code can now run /design-sync in the Claude Code terminal to pull in real design system components or push output back to the canvas, replacing manual copy-paste. Import your Figma token exports or GitHub design-system package to get brand-consistent prototypes.

items.headline: Google launches Veo 3.1 in Gemini API as Veo 3.0 endpoints reach 10-day shutdown window
items.description: Google launched Veo 3.1 and Veo 3.1 Fast in paid preview via the Gemini API on June 18, replacing the Veo 3.0 generation. The legacy model IDs veo-3.0-generate-001 and veo-3.0-fast-generate-001 are now deprecated with a hard shutdown on June 30, 2026. The Veo 3.1 models are also available as GA via the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and Vertex AI.
items.action: Update any integration calling veo-3.0-generate-001 or veo-3.0-fast-generate-001 to the new Veo 3.1 model IDs before June 30 to avoid service interruption.

2026-06-21.summary: Anthropic Workload Identity Federation goes generally available, replacing static API keys with short-lived OIDC tokens for every Claude API endpoint and Claude Code integration.

items.headline: Anthropic WIF goes GA letting any OIDC workload authenticate to Claude without a static API key
items.description: Workload Identity Federation (WIF) is now generally available on the Claude Platform, announced June 17. Workloads present a signed JWT from AWS IAM, GCP service accounts, Azure Managed Identity, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, SPIFFE, or Okta and receive a short-lived Anthropic access token in return, with no static sk-ant-* key required. The release introduces service accounts so each workload has its own identity, roles, and audit trail, and adds Admin API endpoints for programmatic federation rule management across multi-workspace deployments.
items.action: Migrate CI/CD pipelines and background agents from long-lived API keys to OIDC-backed service accounts. GitHub Actions workloads can enable keyless auth in minutes using the official federation rule template. Existing API keys remain valid in parallel during migration.

2026-06-22.summary: LiteLLM unauthenticated RCE chain hits CISA federal patching deadline; Fable 5 exits subscription free window for credit billing; Claude Mythos Preview retires June 30 with its only replacement still suspended.

items.headline: LiteLLM unauthenticated RCE chain reaches CISA federal patching deadline
items.description: CVE-2026-42271 (CVSS 8.7, command injection via /mcp-rest/test endpoints) chains with CVE-2026-48710 (Starlette BadHost host-header bypass) to achieve full unauthenticated RCE against LiteLLM AI Gateway deployments, combined CVSS 10.0. CISA added the exploit to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 8 with a June 22 federal compliance deadline; Horizon3.ai confirmed active exploitation across exposed instances. Affects LiteLLM 1.74.2 through 1.83.6.
items.action: Upgrade LiteLLM to 1.83.7 and Starlette to 1.0.1 immediately. Disable /mcp-rest/test/connection and /mcp-rest/test/tools/list endpoints if immediate patching is not possible. Audit any exposed LiteLLM proxy for signs of compromise.

items.headline: Fable 5 exits free subscription window starting June 23
items.description: From June 9 through today (June 22), Claude Fable 5 was included at no extra cost on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. Starting June 23, usage draws on credits billed at $10 per million input and $50 per million output tokens, double Opus 4.8 pricing. The model remains suspended under the June 12 US export control directive and is not currently accessible on any plan.
items.action: Budget for Fable 5 usage credits going forward. When the export control is lifted and Fable 5 returns, it will no longer be covered by plan limits, so any workflow relying on it will incur per-token charges from day one of restoration.

items.headline: Claude Mythos Preview retires June 30 with replacement still under export ban
items.description: Anthropic's model deprecations page confirms claude-mythos-preview retires on June 30, 2026, eight days from now. The listed migration target is claude-mythos-5, which remains inaccessible under the June 12 export control suspension. Organizations with Project Glasswing access using the preview API identifier face a hard cutoff with no functioning fallback model unless the suspension is lifted before the deadline.
items.action: If your stack calls claude-mythos-preview, contact Anthropic support now to understand options. Monitor the export control resolution timeline closely; if the suspension extends past June 30, Glasswing preview integrations will break.

2026-06-23.summary: Transformer co-author Noam Shazeer leaves Google to lead OpenAI architecture research; Anthropic ships live team Artifacts for Claude Code; Claude Code 2.1.186 adds MCP auth CLI commands and bash auto-response.

items.headline: Transformer co-author Shazeer leaves Google to head OpenAI architecture research
items.description: Noam Shazeer, Google VP of Engineering and Gemini co-lead, announced June 17 that he is joining OpenAI as Head of Architecture Research. Shazeer co-authored the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper that introduced the transformer and was brought back to Google from Character.AI via a $2.7 billion deal in 2024. The move is the single largest talent shift from Google DeepMind to a rival since that deal was struck, and hands OpenAI a foundational architect of the transformer era at a moment when architectural efficiency is the primary cost lever in model deployment.
items.action: Track architectural changes in OpenAI models over the next 12 to 18 months. The last time Shazeer ran architecture research he rewrote Character.AI inference from scratch for latency. Expect OpenAI to accelerate work on MoE routing, speculative decoding, and sub-quadratic attention variants. Gemini model velocity may slow as Google backfills.

items.headline: Claude Code Artifacts turns coding sessions into live shareable dashboards for teams
items.description: Anthropic launched Artifacts for Claude Code in beta on June 18 for Team and Enterprise plans, accessible from both CLI and desktop app. Each Claude Code session can now emit a live, interactive HTML page at a shareable URL that updates in real time as the agent works, making dashboards, app prototypes, and data views visible to teammates without requiring them to join the terminal session. Pages are hosted by Anthropic and viewable in any browser.
items.action: Test for internal tooling: project status pages fed by autonomous Claude Code runs, data visualizations that update as Claude rewrites queries, and handoff artifacts for stakeholders who do not use the CLI. The real-time update model makes this a lightweight alternative to deploying an internal dashboard app for team-facing agent outputs.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.186 adds MCP server auth CLI commands and bash auto-response mode
items.description: Released June 22 at 20:37 UTC, v2.1.186 introduces `claude mcp login <name>` and `claude mcp logout <name>` commands for authenticating MCP servers without opening the interactive menu, enabling non-interactive CI flows for MCP-gated tools. Bash commands prefixed with `!` now automatically trigger Claude responses by default, configurable via `respondToBashCommands: false`. Background subagents no longer silently auto-deny permission prompts but surface them in the main session instead.
items.action: Use the new MCP auth commands to script authenticated MCP server setup in CI pipelines. Review `respondToBashCommands` if you use `!` commands in automated contexts where the auto-response would be unexpected. The subagent permission surfacing change means unattended agents will pause for human review rather than proceeding with deny, which reduces silent failures but requires operator attention.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.142.0 stable ships token budgets for agent threads and multi-agent delegation
items.description: The first stable release in the 0.142.x series shipped June 22 at 22:19 UTC with configurable token budgets per agent thread, multi-agent delegation options, and an indexed web-search mode. The plugin catalog is reorganized into curated, workspace, and shared sections with a new usage limit reset flow including confirmation and retry.
items.action: Evaluate token budgets for cost-capped multi-step agent runs where you need hard spending limits per task. Multi-agent delegation lets a Codex orchestrator hand sub-tasks to specialized threads, which is useful for parallel code review or split-path testing workflows.

2026-06-24.summary: OpenAI launches GPT-5.5-Cyber and Patch the Planet to fix open-source vulnerabilities at scale; Gemini image preview models shut down tomorrow June 25.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.5-Cyber and Patch the Planet to secure open-source at scale
items.description: OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program with the full release of GPT-5.5-Cyber (85.6% on CyberGym, highest single-model score) and Patch the Planet, a new initiative with Trail of Bits, HackerOne, and Calif to fund expert security researchers working directly with open-source maintainers. Initial participating projects include cURL, Python, Go, aiohttp, Sigstore, and pyca/cryptography across more than 30 projects. A five-day initial sprint surfaced hundreds of issues, merged dozens of patches, and produced reusable fuzzing tooling that projects keep permanently.
items.action: If your stack depends on any of the 30-plus enrolled open-source projects, monitor their changelogs for AI-assisted security patches landing over the coming weeks. GPT-5.5-Cyber is available via Codex Security for organizations in the Trusted Access for Cyber program.

items.headline: Gemini image preview models shut down tomorrow June 25 as GA replacements go live
items.description: Google shuts down gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview and gemini-3-pro-image-preview from the Gemini API at midnight June 25. GA replacements gemini-3.1-flash-image and gemini-3-pro-image (Nano Banana 2 and Nano Banana Pro) are already available. Any application still calling the preview model strings will begin returning errors after tonight.
items.action: Update all API calls from gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview to gemini-3.1-flash-image and from gemini-3-pro-image-preview to gemini-3-pro-image before June 25. Test GA behavior before cutoff as pricing and rate limits may differ from preview.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.187 adds sandbox credential blocking and org-level model restrictions
items.description: Claude Code 2.1.187 ships a new sandbox.credentials setting that blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables, reducing the blast radius of compromised tool calls in multi-agent deployments. A new org-configured model restriction enforces permitted model limits on the model picker, --model, /model, and ANTHROPIC_MODEL flags. Remote MCP tool calls that stall no longer hang for five minutes but now abort with an error, configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT.
items.action: Set sandbox.credentials in project settings to harden shared or multi-tenant Claude Code deployments. Enterprise admins can centrally block specific models from org-wide Claude Code sessions via org policy.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.64 stable ships inline image rendering and expanded worktree support
items.description: GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.64 is the first stable release in the 1.0.64 series following four pre-release builds on June 22-23. Key additions include inline image rendering directly in the CLI, expanded worktree functionality for parallel branch workflows, websocket response support for custom OpenAI API-compatible providers, and improved session resumption stability.
items.action: Update via your package manager. If you use custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints with Copilot CLI, the new websocket response support may reduce latency on streaming responses.

2026-06-25.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Tag as a persistent AI teammate inside Slack while OpenAI expands ChatGPT Enterprise write access to the same platform; Gemini image preview APIs retire today and GPT-4.5 exits ChatGPT in 48 hours.

items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Tag as persistent AI teammate inside Slack with ambient mode and shared enterprise identity
items.description: Claude Tag replaces the existing Claude for Slack app and lets Enterprise and Team customers add a shared Claude identity to channels where it learns the organization, breaks delegated tasks into stages, and delivers results asynchronously. An ambient mode proactively resurfaces stalled threads and pushes context updates without being explicitly summoned. Administrators control per-team tool access, spending limits, and channel scope; separate Claude identities keep engineering and sales contexts isolated by design.
items.action: Evaluate Claude Tag for teams that coordinate in Slack. Administrators on Team or Enterprise plans can opt in and migrate from the old Claude Slack app within a 30-day window with launch credits available.

items.headline: Gemini image preview models retire today as GA versions with video-to-image generation go live
items.description: gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview and gemini-3-pro-image-preview are shut down effective June 25. The GA replacements are gemini-3.1-flash-image and gemini-3-pro-image. The flash image GA model adds a new capability: passing a video file as multimodal context to generate thumbnails, cinematic posters, or summary infographics.
items.action: Update API calls referencing the preview model IDs by dropping the '-preview' suffix. Calls to the old strings return errors from today. The video-to-image capability on gemini-3.1-flash-image is available immediately.

items.headline: GPT-4.5 exits ChatGPT in 48 hours on June 27, API access unaffected
items.description: OpenAI retires GPT-4.5 from ChatGPT on June 27 following a 30-day sunset period, completing the removal of the GPT-4 generation from the ChatGPT interface. The retirement applies to ChatGPT paid plans only; the model remains accessible via API key with no announced API deprecation date. OpenAI o3 follows in a separate sunset on August 26.
items.action: Switch any ChatGPT workflows that rely on model picker selection of GPT-4.5 to GPT-5.5 or GPT-5.4 before June 27. API usage requires no action.

items.headline: ChatGPT Enterprise gains Slack write actions with channel, reminder, file, and profile operations
items.description: A June 22 connector update gives ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu workspaces the ability to take write actions inside Slack: joining channels, creating reminders, uploading files, and updating user profiles. Write actions are disabled by default and require administrator activation, giving IT teams control before automation runs. The update positions OpenAI's Slack integration one day before Anthropic launched Claude Tag with broader ambient mode and persistent memory capabilities.
items.action: Enterprise and Edu administrators can enable Slack write actions under Workspace Settings. Compare write-action scope and memory capabilities against Claude Tag before committing platform-wide.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.191 adds session rewind from before clear and cuts streaming CPU by 37 percent
items.description: /rewind now lets users resume a conversation from the exact state before /clear was called, recovering context that would otherwise be lost permanently. Text update coalescing at 100ms intervals cuts CPU usage during streaming responses by approximately 37 percent. MCP server connections gain automatic retry logic for transient network errors, reducing spurious disconnection failures in multi-server setups.
items.action: Update Claude Code. Teams running multiple MCP servers see fewer disconnects without configuration changes; /rewind is valuable in long sessions where accidental /clear has cost context.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.65 ships persistent working directory and skill management subcommand
items.description: v1.0.65 (June 24 stable, first release after v1.0.64 covered June 24) adds /cd with state persistence so the working directory carries forward across subsequent shell operations without re-navigation. A new /skill subcommand manages installed skills directly inside the CLI. Canvas resume reliability is fixed and CI status is now visible inline.
items.action: Update to v1.0.65. The /cd persistence benefits workflows using sequential shell operations in different directories; /skill simplifies managing Claude Code skills from within a Copilot session.

2026-06-26.summary: Claude Code gains auto-mode shell classifier controls and bash path autocomplete while OpenAI unveils its first custom inference chip with Broadcom and ships a new zsh shell integration for Codex CLI.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.193 adds auto-mode shell classifier bash path autocomplete and MCP auth reconnect
items.description: A new autoMode.classifyAllShell setting routes all Bash and PowerShell commands through the auto-mode classifier, normalizing approval behavior across command types. Auto-mode denial reasons now surface in transcripts and the denial toast, giving audit logs a clear record of blocked operations. Live file path autocomplete activates in bash mode via the ! shortcut, an MCP startup notice flags servers requiring authentication before session start, and headersHelper MCP auth reconnects automatically on 401 or 403 errors.
items.action: Update Claude Code to 2.1.193. Enable autoMode.classifyAllShell in CLAUDE.md if you need consistent approval behavior across mixed shell environments; the MCP 401/403 auto-reconnect removes manual intervention in multi-server workflows.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils Jalapeño custom ASIC with Broadcom targeting gigawatt scale inference by end of 2026
items.description: OpenAI's first proprietary inference chip, co-designed with Broadcom over nine months, reached tape-out and is running engineering samples at production frequency. The architecture targets LLM inference kernels, memory movement, and high-bandwidth networking, with substantially better performance per watt than current alternatives. OpenAI used its own models to accelerate the chip design process; production deployment is targeted at gigawatt-scale data centers by end of 2026, with capacity expanding in subsequent years.
items.action: Track the Jalapeño rollout as a signal for lower OpenAI API costs and higher throughput ceilings from 2027 onward. No immediate workflow changes required.

items.headline: Codex CLI 0.142.2 defaults MCP tools to search mode and ships first zsh shell integration
items.description: Version 0.142.2 (June 25) sets MCP tools to default to tool search when supported, streamlining initial workflow for multi-server setups; macOS auth now honors the system proxy and plugin catalogs return curated featured rankings. Separately, codex-zsh v0.1.0 (June 25) is the first release of the Codex zsh shell integration, enabling inline AI assistance directly from the zsh prompt without switching windows.
items.action: Update Codex CLI to 0.142.2 and install codex-zsh if you run zsh and want inline Codex queries at the shell prompt.
